verses.1:1: The book of the lineage of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham.
verses.1:2: Abraham fathered Isaac, and Isaac fathered Jacob, and Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers.
verses.1:3: Judah fathered Perez and Zerah by Tamar, and Perez fathered Hezron, and Hezron fathered Ram.
verses.1:4: Ram fathered Amminadab, and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon.
verses.1:5: Salmon fathered Boaz by Rahab, and Boaz fathered Obed by Ruth, and Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David the king.
verses.1:6: David the king fathered Solomon by her who had been Uriah's.
verses.1:7: Solomon fathered Rehoboam, and Rehoboam fathered Abijah, and Abijah fathered Asa.
verses.1:8: Asa fathered Jehoshaphat, and Jehoshaphat fathered Joram, and Joram fathered Uzziah.
verses.1:9: Uzziah fathered Jotham, and Jotham fathered Ahaz, and Ahaz fathered Hezekiah.
verses.1:10: Hezekiah fathered Manasseh, and Manasseh fathered Amon, and Amon fathered Josiah.
verses.1:11: Josiah fathered Jeconiah and his brothers during the deportation to Babylon.
verses.1:12: And after the deportation to Babylon, Jeconiah fathered Shealtiel, and Shealtiel fathered Zerubbabel.
verses.1:13: Zerubbabel fathered Abiud, and Abiud fathered Eliakim, and Eliakim fathered Azor.
verses.1:14: Azor fathered Zadok, and Zadok fathered Achim, and Achim fathered Eliud.
verses.1:15: Eliud fathered Eleazar, and Eleazar fathered Matthan, and Matthan fathered Jacob.
verses.1:16: Jacob fathered Joseph, the husband of Mary, from whom Jesus was born, who is called Christ.
verses.1:17: Therefore all the generations from Abraham up to David are fourteen generations; and from David up to the deportation to Babylon, fourteen generations; and from the deportation to Babylon up to Christ, fourteen generations.
verses.1:18: Now the birth of Christ was in this manner: when His mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph, before they came together, she was found pregnant from the Holy Spirit.
verses.1:19: Now Joseph, her husband, since he was righteous and did not wish to expose her publicly, intended to send her away secretly.
verses.1:20: While he was pondering these things, look, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, "Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, for what has been conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
verses.1:21: And she will bear a son, and you will call His name Jesus, for He Himself will save His people from their sins."
verses.1:22: Now all this happened so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying,
verses.1:23: "Look, the virgin will be pregnant and will bear a son, and they will call His name Emmanuel," which is translated, "God with us."
verses.1:24: Now Joseph, rising from sleep, did as the angel of the Lord commanded him, and took his wife.
verses.1:25: And he did not know her until she bore her firstborn son, and he called His name Jesus.
verses.2:1: Therefore, when Jesus had been born in Bethlehem of Judah in the days of King Herod, look, magi from the east came to Jerusalem,
verses.2:2: saying, "Where is the One born King of the Jews? For we saw His star in the east, and we came to worship Him."
verses.2:3: Now on hearing this, King Herod was disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him.
verses.2:4: And assembling all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he inquired of them where the Christ was to be born.
verses.2:5: And they said, "In Bethlehem of Judah, for thus it is written through the prophet:
verses.2:6: 'And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for from you will come forth a leader who will rule My people Israel.'"
verses.2:7: Then Herod, having secretly summoned the magi, carefully learned from them the time of the star that appeared to them.
verses.2:8: And sending them to Bethlehem, he said, "Go and inquire carefully concerning the child; and when you have found Him, report back to me, so that I too may come and worship Him."
verses.2:9: After they had heard the king, they departed; and look, the star that they had seen in the east was going ahead of them, until it came and stood above where the child was.
verses.2:10: And when they saw the star, they rejoiced with very great joy.
verses.2:11: And entering the house, they found the child with Mary His mother, and falling down, they worshiped Him; and opening their treasures, they offered Him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
verses.2:12: And having received an answer in a dream not to return to Herod, they went back to their own region by another way.
verses.2:13: Now when they had departed, look, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, "Get up, take the child and His mother, and flee into Egypt, and remain there until I tell you. For Herod is about to search for the child to destroy Him."
verses.2:14: So rising up, he took the child and His mother by night and withdrew into Egypt,
verses.2:15: and he was there until the death of Herod, so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying, "From Egypt I called My Son."
verses.2:16: Then Herod, seeing that he had been tricked by the magi, became very angry; and he sent and killed all the boys who were in Bethlehem and in all its districts, from two years of age and under, according to the time that he had ascertained from the magi.
verses.2:17: Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, saying,
verses.2:18: "A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and much wailing: Rachel weeping for her children, and she was unwilling to be comforted, because they are no more."
verses.2:19: Now when Herod had died, look, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt,
verses.2:20: saying, "Get up, take the child and His mother, and go into the land of Israel; for those who were seeking the child's life have died."
verses.2:21: So rising up, he took the child and His mother and came into the land of Israel.
verses.2:22: But hearing that Archelaus was reigning in Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there; and being warned in a dream, he withdrew into the districts of Galilee.
verses.2:23: And he came and lived in a city that is called Nazareth, so that what was spoken through the prophets might be fulfilled: "He will be called a Nazarene."
verses.3:1: Now in those days, John the Baptist came preaching in the wilderness of Judea,
verses.3:2: and saying, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near."
verses.3:3: For this is the one spoken of through Isaiah the prophet, saying, "A voice of one crying out in the wilderness: 'Prepare the way of the Lord; make His paths straight.'"
verses.3:4: Now John himself had a garment made of camel hair and a belt of leather around his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.
verses.3:5: Then Jerusalem was going out to him, and all Judea, and all the region around the Jordan,
verses.3:6: and they were being baptized by him in the Jordan, confessing their sins.
verses.3:7: But seeing many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said to them, "Offspring of vipers, who showed you to flee from the wrath to come?
verses.3:8: Therefore produce fruit worthy of repentance.
verses.3:9: And do not wish to say within yourselves, 'We have Abraham as our father.' For I tell you that God is able from these stones to raise up children for Abraham.
verses.3:10: For already the ax has been placed at the root of the trees. Therefore every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.
verses.3:11: I indeed baptize you in water for repentance, but the One who is to come after me is stronger than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry; He Himself will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire.
verses.3:12: His winnowing fork is in His hand, and He will thoroughly cleanse His threshing floor; and He will gather His wheat into the granary, but the chaff He will burn up with unquenchable fire."
verses.3:13: Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan, to John, in order to be baptized by him.
verses.3:14: But John tried to prevent Him, saying, "I ought to be baptized by You, and You come to me?"
verses.3:15: And Jesus, answering, said to him, "Allow it for now, for thus it is proper for us to fulfill all righteousness." Then he allowed Him.
verses.3:16: And having been baptized, Jesus at once came up from the water; and look, the heavens were opened to Him, and He saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming upon Him.
verses.3:17: And look, a voice from the heavens, saying, "This is My beloved Son, in whom I have taken delight."
verses.4:1: Then Jesus was led into the desert by the Spirit, so that He might be tempted by the devil.
verses.4:2: And when He had fasted for forty days and forty nights, afterward He became hungry.
verses.4:3: And approaching, the tempter said to Him, "If You are the Son of God, command that these stones become loaves of bread."
verses.4:4: Responding, He said, "It is written: 'Not on bread alone does man live, but on every word that goes forth from the mouth of God.'"
verses.4:5: Then the devil took Him into the holy city, and placed Him on the pinnacle of the temple,
verses.4:6: and said to Him, "If You are the Son of God, throw Yourself down; for it is written that 'He has commanded His angels concerning You, and in their hands they will lift You up, so that You may not by chance strike Your foot against a stone.'"
verses.4:7: Jesus said to him, "Again, it is written: 'You shall not test the Lord your God.'"
verses.4:8: Again the devil took Him onto an exceedingly high mountain, and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory,
verses.4:9: and said to Him, "I will give all these things to You if, falling down, You worship me."
verses.4:10: Then Jesus said to him, "Go away, Satan! For it is written: 'The Lord your God you shall worship, and Him alone you shall serve.'"
verses.4:11: Then the devil left Him, and look, angels approached and were ministering to Him.
verses.4:12: Now when Jesus had heard that John had been handed over, He withdrew into Galilee;
verses.4:13: and having left the city of Nazareth, He came and lived in Capernaum by the sea, within the territory of Zebulun and Naphtali,
verses.4:14: in order that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled:
verses.4:15: "Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the way of the sea, across the Jordan, Galilee of the nations:
verses.4:16: the people who were sitting in darkness have seen a great light, and for those sitting in the region of the shadow of death, light has dawned on them."
verses.4:17: From then on Jesus began to preach and to say, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near."
verses.4:18: Now, walking beside the Sea of Galilee, Jesus saw two brothers, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea (for they were fishermen),
verses.4:19: and said to them, "Come after Me, and I will make you become fishers of men."
verses.4:20: And at once, having left their nets, they followed Him.
verses.4:21: And proceeding from there, He saw two other brothers, James, son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a boat with Zebedee their father, repairing their nets; and He called them.
verses.4:22: And immediately, having left their nets and their father, they followed Him.
verses.4:23: And Jesus was going around all of Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every illness and every infirmity among the people.
verses.4:24: And His reputation went out into all of Syria, and they brought to Him all who were sick, gripped by various illnesses and torments, and those who had demons, and lunatics, and paralytics, and He cured them;
verses.4:25: and many crowds followed Him from Galilee and the Decapolis, and from Jerusalem, and from Judea, and from across the Jordan.
verses.5:1: Now seeing the crowds, Jesus went up onto the mountain, and when He had sat down, His disciples approached Him.
verses.5:2: And opening His mouth, He was teaching them, saying:
verses.5:3: "Blessed are the poor in spirit, because the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
verses.5:4: Blessed are those who mourn, because they will be comforted.
verses.5:5: Blessed are the meek, because they will possess the earth.
verses.5:6: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, because they will be satisfied.
verses.5:7: Blessed are the merciful, because they will obtain mercy.
verses.5:8: Blessed are the pure in heart, because they will see God.
verses.5:9: Blessed are the peacemakers, because they will be called sons of God.
verses.5:10: Blessed are those who suffer persecution on account of righteousness, because the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
verses.5:11: Blessed are you when they revile you, and persecute you, and falsely say all evil against you on account of Me.
verses.5:12: Rejoice and exult, because your reward is abundant in heaven. For in this way they persecuted the prophets who were before you.
verses.5:13: You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt loses its strength, with what will it be salted? It is good for nothing any longer, except to be thrown outside and trampled by people.
verses.5:14: You are the light of the world. A city placed on a mountain cannot be hidden;
verses.5:15: nor do they light a lamp and put it under a grain measure, but on a lampstand, so that it may shine for all who are in the house.
verses.5:16: In this way let your light shine before people, so that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
verses.5:17: Do not suppose that I have come to annul the law or the prophets; I have not come to annul, but to fulfill.
verses.5:18: For amen, I tell you, until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota or one stroke will pass from the law until all things take place.
verses.5:19: Therefore, whoever annuls one of these least commandments and teaches people so will be called least in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever does and teaches them, this one will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
verses.5:20: For I tell you that unless your righteousness abounds more than that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will not enter into the kingdom of heaven.
verses.5:21: You have heard that it was said to the ancients, 'You shall not kill, and whoever kills will be liable to judgment.'
verses.5:22: But I tell you that everyone who is angry with his brother will be liable to judgment. And whoever says to his brother, 'Raca,' will be liable to the council. And whoever says, 'Fool,' will be liable to the Gehenna of fire.
verses.5:23: Therefore, if you are offering your gift at the altar, and there you remember that your brother has something against you,
verses.5:24: leave your gift there before the altar, and go first to be reconciled to your brother; and then come and offer your gift.
verses.5:25: Be in agreement with your adversary quickly while you are on the way with him, or else the adversary might hand you over to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and you be thrown into prison.
verses.5:26: Amen, I tell you, you will not come out from there until you pay the last quadrans.
verses.5:27: You have heard that it was said to the ancients, 'You shall not commit adultery.'
verses.5:28: But I tell you that everyone who looks at a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
verses.5:29: Now if your right eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish than for your whole body to be thrown into Gehenna.
verses.5:30: And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish than for your whole body to go into Gehenna.
verses.5:31: Now it was said, 'Whoever divorces his wife must give her a document of divorce.'
verses.5:32: But I tell you that everyone who divorces his wife, except for a cause of sexual immorality, causes her to commit adultery; and whoever marries a woman who has been divorced commits adultery.
verses.5:33: Again, you have heard that it was said to the ancients, 'You shall not swear falsely, but you shall fulfill your oaths to the Lord.'
verses.5:34: But I tell you not to swear at all: neither by heaven, because it is the throne of God,
verses.5:35: nor by the earth, because it is the footstool of His feet; nor by Jerusalem, because it is the city of the great King;
verses.5:36: nor shall you swear by your head, because you cannot make one hair white or black.
verses.5:37: But let your speech be, 'Yes, yes,' 'No, no'; and whatever is more than these is from evil.
verses.5:38: You have heard that it was said, 'An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.'
verses.5:39: But I tell you not to resist evil; rather, if anyone strikes you on your right cheek, offer him the other also.
verses.5:40: And to the one who wants to contend with you in court and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well.
verses.5:41: And whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two more.
verses.5:42: Give to whoever asks from you, and do not turn away from the one who wishes to borrow from you.
verses.5:43: You have heard that it was said, 'You shall love your neighbor, and you shall hate your enemy.'
verses.5:44: But I tell you: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who persecute and slander you,
verses.5:45: so that you may be sons of your Father who is in heaven, who makes His sun rise on the good and the evil, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.
verses.5:46: For if you love those who love you, what reward will you have? Do not even the tax collectors do this?
verses.5:47: And if you greet your brothers only, what more do you do? Do not even the Gentiles do this?
verses.5:48: Therefore, you must be perfect, just as your heavenly Father also is perfect."
verses.6:1: "Watch out that you do not practice your righteousness in front of people in order to be seen by them; otherwise you will have no reward with your Father who is in heaven.
verses.6:2: Therefore, when you give alms, do not blow a trumpet ahead of yourself, just as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, so that they may be honored by people. Amen, I tell you, they have received their reward.
verses.6:3: But while you are giving alms, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
verses.6:4: so that your almsgiving may be in secret, and your Father, who sees in secret, will repay you.
verses.6:5: And when you pray, you shall not be like the hypocrites, who love standing in the synagogues and at the corners of the broad streets to pray, so that they may be seen by people. Amen, I tell you, they have received their reward.
verses.6:6: But as for you, when you pray, enter your inner room, and with the door shut, pray to your Father in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will repay you.
verses.6:7: And while praying, do not speak much, like the Gentiles, for they think that through their much speaking they will be heard.
verses.6:8: Therefore do not become like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask Him.
verses.6:9: Therefore you shall pray like this: 'Our Father, who are in heaven, may Your name be sanctified.
verses.6:10: May Your kingdom come; may Your will be done, just as in heaven, also on earth.
verses.6:11: Give us today our supersubstantial bread,
verses.6:12: and forgive us our debts, just as we also forgive our debtors.
verses.6:13: And do not lead us into temptation, but rescue us from evil. Amen.'
verses.6:14: For if you forgive people their sins, your heavenly Father will also forgive you your offenses.
verses.6:15: But if you do not forgive people, neither will your Father forgive you your sins.
verses.6:16: And when you fast, do not become gloomy like the hypocrites. For they disfigure their faces so that they may appear to people to be fasting. Amen, I tell you that they have received their reward.
verses.6:17: But as for you, when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,
verses.6:18: so that you may not appear to people to be fasting, but to your Father who is in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will repay you.
verses.6:19: Do not store up treasures for yourselves on earth, where rust and moth destroy, and where thieves dig through and steal.
verses.6:20: But store up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where neither rust nor moth destroys, and where thieves do not dig through or steal.
verses.6:21: For where your treasure is, there your heart is also.
verses.6:22: The lamp of your body is your eye. If your eye is sound, your whole body will be filled with light.
verses.6:23: But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be filled with darkness. If therefore the light that is in you is darkness, how great will that darkness itself be?
verses.6:24: No one can serve two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will uphold the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon.
verses.6:25: For this reason I tell you: do not be anxious for your life, what you will eat, nor for your body, what you will put on. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
verses.6:26: Look at the birds of the sky, for they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth much more than they?
verses.6:27: And which of you, by thinking, can add one cubit to his stature?
verses.6:28: And why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin.
verses.6:29: Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
verses.6:30: But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more you, you of little faith?
verses.6:31: Therefore do not be anxious, saying, 'What will we eat, or what will we drink, or with what will we be clothed?'
verses.6:32: For the nations seek after all these things. For your Father knows that you need all these things.
verses.6:33: So then, seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.
verses.6:34: Therefore do not be anxious for tomorrow. For tomorrow's day will be anxious for itself; its own trouble is enough for the day."
verses.7:1: "Do not pass judgment, so that you may not be judged.
verses.7:2: For with the judgment by which you judge, you will be judged; and with the measure by which you measure, it will be measured back to you.
verses.7:3: And why do you see the splinter in your brother's eye, yet do not see the beam in your own eye?
verses.7:4: Or how do you say to your brother, 'Let me remove the splinter from your eye,' when look, a beam is in your own eye?
verses.7:5: Hypocrite, first remove the beam from your own eye, and then you will see to remove the splinter from your brother's eye.
verses.7:6: Do not give what is holy to dogs, nor throw your pearls in front of pigs; otherwise they might trample them under their feet and, turning around, tear you to pieces.
verses.7:7: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened for you.
verses.7:8: For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and for the one knocking it will be opened.
verses.7:9: Or what man is there among you who, if his son asks him for bread, would hand him a stone?
verses.7:10: Or if he asks for a fish, would he hand him a snake?
verses.7:11: If therefore you, though you are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father, who is in heaven, give good things to those who ask Him?
verses.7:12: Therefore, everything that you want people to do for you, you also do for them; for this is the Law and the Prophets.
verses.7:13: Enter through the narrow gate, because wide is the gate and spacious is the road that leads to destruction, and many are those who enter through it.
verses.7:14: How narrow is the gate and constricted is the road that leads to life, and few are those who find it!
verses.7:15: Watch out for false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing, yet inwardly they are ravenous wolves.
verses.7:16: By their fruits you will recognize them. Do people gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles?
verses.7:17: In this way every good tree produces good fruits, while a bad tree produces bad fruits.
verses.7:18: A good tree cannot produce bad fruits, nor can a bad tree produce good fruits.
verses.7:19: Every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.
verses.7:20: So then, from their fruits you will recognize them.
verses.7:21: Not everyone who says to Me, 'Lord, Lord,' will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of My Father, who is in heaven, he himself will enter the kingdom of heaven.
verses.7:22: Many will say to Me on that day, 'Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Your name, and in Your name cast out demons, and in Your name perform many mighty works?'
verses.7:23: And then I will declare to them, 'I never knew you; depart from Me, you who practice iniquity.'
verses.7:24: Therefore everyone who hears these words of Mine and does them will be likened to a wise man who built his house upon the rock.
verses.7:25: And the rain came down, and the floods came, and the winds blew and rushed against that house, and it did not fall, for it had been founded upon the rock.
verses.7:26: And everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not do them will be like a foolish man who built his house upon the sand.
verses.7:27: And the rain came down, and the floods came, and the winds blew and rushed against that house, and it fell, and its ruin was great."
verses.7:28: And it happened, when Jesus had finished these words, that the crowds were amazed at His teaching.
verses.7:29: For He was teaching them as one having authority, and not like their scribes and the Pharisees.
verses.8:1: Now when He had come down from the mountain, large crowds followed Him.
verses.8:2: And look, a leper came up and worshiped Him, saying, "Lord, if You wish, You are able to cleanse me."
verses.8:3: And stretching out His hand, Jesus touched him, saying, "I wish it; be cleansed." And at once his leprosy was cleansed.
verses.8:4: And Jesus said to him, "See to it that you tell no one, but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses prescribed, as a testimony to them."
verses.8:5: Now when He had entered Capernaum, a centurion approached Him, pleading with Him,
verses.8:6: and saying, "Lord, my boy lies paralyzed in the house and is severely tormented."
verses.8:7: And Jesus said to him, "I will come and cure him."
verses.8:8: And answering, the centurion said, "Lord, I am not worthy for You to enter under my roof, but only speak a word, and my boy will be healed.
verses.8:9: For I also am a man placed under authority, having soldiers under me; and I say to this one, 'Go,' and he goes; and to another, 'Come,' and he comes; and to my servant, 'Do this,' and he does it."
verses.8:10: Now hearing this, Jesus marveled, and He said to those following Him, "Amen, I tell you, I have not found such great faith in Israel.
verses.8:11: And I say to you that many will come from east and west, and will recline with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven,
verses.8:12: but the sons of the kingdom will be cast out into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth."
verses.8:13: And Jesus said to the centurion, "Go, and just as you have believed, let it be done for you." And the boy was healed in that hour.
verses.8:14: And when Jesus had come into Peter's house, He saw his mother-in-law lying down and having a fever.
verses.8:15: And He touched her hand, and the fever left her; and she rose and was serving them.
verses.8:16: Now when evening had come, they brought to Him many who had demons; and He was casting out the spirits with a word, and He cured all who were ill,
verses.8:17: so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, saying, "He Himself took our infirmities and carried our illnesses."
verses.8:18: Now Jesus, seeing large crowds around Him, gave orders to go across the water.
verses.8:19: And one scribe approached and said to Him, "Teacher, I will follow You wherever You go."
verses.8:20: And Jesus said to him, "Foxes have dens and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to rest His head."
verses.8:21: And another of His disciples said to Him, "Lord, permit me first to go and bury my father."
verses.8:22: But Jesus said to him, "Follow Me, and let the dead bury their own dead."
verses.8:23: And as He stepped into the boat, His disciples followed Him.
verses.8:24: And look, a great upheaval arose on the sea, so that the boat was being covered by the waves; but He Himself was sleeping.
verses.8:25: And His disciples approached Him and roused Him, saying, "Lord, save us; we are perishing!"
verses.8:26: And Jesus said to them, "Why are you fearful, you of little faith?" Then rising, He commanded the winds and the sea, and a great calm came about.
verses.8:27: Moreover, the men marveled, saying, "What sort of man is this, that the winds and the sea obey Him?"
verses.8:28: And when He had come across the water into the region of the Gerasenes, two men who had demons met Him, coming out of the tombs, exceedingly fierce, so that no one could pass along that road.
verses.8:29: And look, they cried out, saying, "What is there between us and You, Jesus, Son of God? Have You come here before the time to torment us?"
verses.8:30: Now not far from them there was a herd of many pigs feeding.
verses.8:31: And the demons were pleading with Him, saying, "If You cast us out from here, send us into the herd of pigs."
verses.8:32: And He said to them, "Go." And coming out, they went into the pigs; and look, the whole herd rushed down the steep slope into the sea, and they died in the waters.
verses.8:33: Now the herdsmen fled, and coming into the city, they reported everything, and about those who had had demons.
verses.8:34: And look, the whole city went out to meet Jesus; and upon seeing Him, they pleaded that He would depart from their borders.
verses.9:1: And stepping into the boat, He crossed over the water and came into His own city.
verses.9:2: And look, they were bringing to Him a paralytic lying on a bed. And seeing their faith, Jesus said to the paralytic, "Have courage, son; your sins are forgiven you."
verses.9:3: And look, some of the scribes said within themselves, "This man is blaspheming."
verses.9:4: And when Jesus had seen their thoughts, He said, "Why do you think evil things in your hearts?
verses.9:5: Which is easier, to say, 'Your sins are forgiven you,' or to say, 'Rise and walk'?
verses.9:6: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins," then He said to the paralytic, "Rise, pick up your bed, and go to your house."
verses.9:7: And he rose and went away to his house.
verses.9:8: Now when the crowds saw this, they were afraid, and they glorified God, who gave such authority to men.
verses.9:9: And as Jesus was passing on from there, He saw a man sitting at the tax office, Matthew by name. And He said to him, "Follow Me." And rising, he followed Him.
verses.9:10: And it happened that, as He was reclining at table in the house, look, many tax collectors and sinners came and were reclining at table with Jesus and His disciples.
verses.9:11: And seeing this, the Pharisees were saying to His disciples, "Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?"
verses.9:12: But Jesus, hearing this, said, "A physician is not needed by the healthy, but by those who are ill.
verses.9:13: But go and learn what this means: 'Mercy I desire, and not sacrifice.' For I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners."
verses.9:14: Then the disciples of John approached Him, saying, "Why do we and the Pharisees fast frequently, but Your disciples do not fast?"
verses.9:15: And Jesus said to them, "Can the sons of the bridegroom mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them? Yet days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast.
verses.9:16: Moreover, no one puts a patch of raw cloth onto an old garment; for it takes away its fullness from the garment, and a worse tear is made.
verses.9:17: Nor do they put new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wineskins burst, and the wine is poured out, and the wineskins perish. But they put new wine into new wineskins, and both are preserved."
verses.9:18: While He was speaking these things to them, look, a certain ruler approached and worshiped Him, saying, "Lord, my daughter has just now died; but come, lay Your hand on her, and she will live."
verses.9:19: And rising, Jesus was following him, and so were His disciples.
verses.9:20: And look, a woman who had been suffering a flow of blood for twelve years approached from behind and touched the fringe of His garment.
verses.9:21: For she was saying within herself, "If I only touch His garment, I will be made whole."
verses.9:22: But Jesus, turning around and seeing her, said, "Have courage, daughter; your faith has made you whole." And the woman was made whole from that hour.
verses.9:23: And when Jesus had come into the ruler's house and had seen the flute players and the crowd making an uproar, He said:
verses.9:24: "Withdraw, for the girl is not dead, but is sleeping." And they were laughing at Him.
verses.9:25: And when the crowd had been driven out, He went in and took hold of her hand, and the girl rose.
verses.9:26: And this report went out into all that land.
verses.9:27: And as Jesus was passing on from there, two blind men followed Him, crying out and saying, "Have mercy on us, Son of David!"
verses.9:28: Now when He had come into the house, the blind men approached Him. And Jesus said to them, "Do you believe that I am able to do this for you?" They said to Him, "Yes, Lord."
verses.9:29: Then He touched their eyes, saying, "According to your faith, let it be done for you."
verses.9:30: And their eyes were opened; and Jesus sternly warned them, saying, "See to it that no one knows."
verses.9:31: But going out, they spread His fame in all that land.
verses.9:32: Now when they had gone out, look, they brought to Him a mute man who had a demon.
verses.9:33: And when the demon had been cast out, the mute man spoke; and the crowds marveled, saying, "Never has anything like this appeared in Israel."
verses.9:34: But the Pharisees were saying, "By the ruler of demons He casts out demons."
verses.9:35: And Jesus was going about all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and curing every sickness and every infirmity.
verses.9:36: Now seeing the crowds, He had compassion on them, because they were harassed and lying prostrate, like sheep having no shepherd.
verses.9:37: Then He said to His disciples, "The harvest indeed is plentiful, but the laborers are few.
verses.9:38: Therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send laborers into His harvest."
verses.10:1: And having summoned His twelve disciples, He gave them authority over unclean spirits, to drive them out and to heal every disease and every infirmity.
verses.10:2: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these: first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother;
verses.10:3: James son of Zebedee, and John his brother; Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James son of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus;
verses.10:4: Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, who also handed Him over.
verses.10:5: These twelve Jesus sent out, instructing them and saying, "Do not go away onto the road of the Gentiles, and do not enter the cities of the Samaritans;
verses.10:6: but rather go to the sheep of the house of Israel that have been lost.
verses.10:7: And as you go, proclaim, saying, 'The kingdom of heaven has drawn near.'
verses.10:8: Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, drive out demons; without cost you have received, without cost give.
verses.10:9: Do not possess gold, nor silver, nor money in your belts;
verses.10:10: no bag on the way, nor two tunics, nor sandals, nor a staff; for the worker is worthy of his food.
verses.10:11: Now into whatever city or village you enter, inquire who in it is worthy, and stay there until you depart.
verses.10:12: And as you enter the house, greet it, saying, 'Peace to this house.'
verses.10:13: And if indeed that house is worthy, your peace will come upon it; but if it is not worthy, your peace will return to you.
verses.10:14: And whoever does not receive you, nor hear your words, as you go outside from the house or city, shake off the dust from your feet.
verses.10:15: Amen, I tell you: It will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that city.
verses.10:16: Look, I am sending you like sheep in the midst of wolves. Therefore be prudent like serpents, and innocent like doves.
verses.10:17: Now be on guard against people. For they will hand you over in councils, and in their synagogues they will flog you;
verses.10:18: and you will be led before governors and before kings on account of Me, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.
verses.10:19: But when they hand you over, do not think about how or what you are to speak; for it will be given to you in that hour what you are to speak;
verses.10:20: for it is not you who are speaking, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you.
verses.10:21: Now brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his son; and children will rise up against parents and put them to death;
verses.10:22: and you will be hated by all on account of My name; but the one who perseveres all the way to the end will be saved.
verses.10:23: Now when they persecute you in this city, flee into another. Amen, I tell you, you will not finish the cities of Israel until the Son of Man comes.
verses.10:24: A disciple is not above the teacher, nor a servant above his master;
verses.10:25: it is enough for the disciple to be like his teacher, and for the servant to be like his master. If they have called the head of the household Beelzebub, how much more those of his household?
verses.10:26: Therefore do not fear them. For nothing is covered that will not be revealed, nor hidden that will not be known.
verses.10:27: What I tell you in the darkness, speak in the light; and what you hear in the ear, proclaim upon the rooftops.
verses.10:28: And do not fear those who kill the body, yet cannot kill the soul; but rather fear Him who is able to destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
verses.10:29: Are not two sparrows sold for a copper coin? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground without your Father.
verses.10:30: Now all the hairs of your head are numbered.
verses.10:31: Therefore do not fear: you are better than many sparrows.
verses.10:32: Therefore everyone who confesses Me in the presence of people, I too will confess him in the presence of My Father who is in heaven.
verses.10:33: But whoever denies Me in the presence of people, I too will deny him in the presence of My Father who is in heaven.
verses.10:34: Do not suppose that I have come to send peace onto the earth; I have not come to send peace, but a sword;
verses.10:35: for I have come to separate a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law;
verses.10:36: and a man's enemies are those of his household.
verses.10:37: The one who loves father or mother more than Me is not worthy of Me; and the one who loves son or daughter above Me is not worthy of Me.
verses.10:38: And the one who does not take his cross and follow Me is not worthy of Me.
verses.10:39: The one who finds his life will lose it, and the one who loses his life on account of Me will find it.
verses.10:40: The one who receives you receives Me, and the one who receives Me receives Him who sent Me.
verses.10:41: The one who receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will obtain the reward of a prophet, and the one who receives a righteous person in the name of a righteous person will obtain the reward of a righteous person.
verses.10:42: And whoever gives one of these least ones only a cup of cold water to drink in the name of a disciple, amen, I tell you, he will not lose his reward."
verses.11:1: And it happened that when Jesus had finished instructing His twelve disciples, He departed from there to teach and to proclaim in their cities.
verses.11:2: Now when John heard in chains about the works of Christ, sending two of his disciples,
verses.11:3: he said to Him, "Are You the One who is to come, or are we waiting for another?"
verses.11:4: And answering, Jesus said to them, "Go and report to John what you have heard and seen.
verses.11:5: The blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead rise, the poor have the good news proclaimed to them;
verses.11:6: and blessed is the one who is not caused to stumble over Me."
verses.11:7: Now as they were departing, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: "What did you go out into the desert to see? A reed swayed by the wind?
verses.11:8: But what did you go out to see? A man clothed in soft garments? Look, those who wear soft garments are in the houses of kings.
verses.11:9: But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
verses.11:10: For this is the one about whom it is written, 'Look, I am sending My messenger before Your face, who will prepare Your way before You.'
verses.11:11: Amen, I tell you, among those born of women no one greater than John the Baptist has arisen; yet whoever is lesser in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he is.
verses.11:12: Now from the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and the violent seize it.
verses.11:13: For all the prophets and the Law prophesied until John;
verses.11:14: and if you are willing to receive it, he himself is Elijah, who is to come.
verses.11:15: The one who has ears to hear, let him hear.
verses.11:16: Now what will I judge this generation to be like? It is like children sitting in the marketplace, who, calling out to their peers,
verses.11:17: say, 'We played music for you, and you did not dance; we lamented, and you did not mourn.'
verses.11:18: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, 'He has a demon.'
verses.11:19: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, 'Look, a gluttonous man and a drinker of wine, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.' And wisdom has been justified by her children."
verses.11:20: Then He began to reproach the cities in which most of His mighty deeds had been done, because they had not repented:
verses.11:21: "Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty deeds that were done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would long ago have repented in sackcloth and ashes.
verses.11:22: Nevertheless, I tell you: It will be more lenient for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.
verses.11:23: And you, Capernaum, will you really be exalted all the way to heaven? You will descend all the way to the underworld. For if the mighty deeds that were done in you had been done in Sodom, perhaps it would have remained until this day.
verses.11:24: Nevertheless, I tell you that it will be more lenient for the land of Sodom on the day of judgment than for you."
verses.11:25: At that time Jesus answered and said, "I give praise to You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and prudent, and have revealed them to little ones.
verses.11:26: Yes, Father, because thus it was pleasing before You.
verses.11:27: Everything has been handed over to Me by My Father. And no one knows the Son except the Father; neither does anyone know the Father except the Son and the one to whom the Son wishes to reveal Him.
verses.11:28: Come to Me, all of you who toil and are weighed down, and I will refresh you.
verses.11:29: Take My yoke upon yourselves and learn from Me, because I am gentle and humble of heart; and you will find rest for your souls.
verses.11:30: For My yoke is pleasant, and My burden is light."
verses.12:1: At that time Jesus went through the sown fields on the Sabbath, and His disciples, being hungry, began to pluck heads of grain and eat.
verses.12:2: Now the Pharisees, seeing this, said to Him, "Look, Your disciples are doing what is not lawful to do on the Sabbath."
verses.12:3: But He said to them, "Have you not read what David did when he was hungry, and those who were with him:
verses.12:4: how he entered into the house of God and ate the loaves of presentation, which it was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those who were with him, except for the priests alone?
verses.12:5: Or have you not read in the Law that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple violate the Sabbath and are without guilt?
verses.12:6: Yet I say to you that One greater than the temple is here.
verses.12:7: But if you knew what this means, 'Mercy I desire, and not sacrifice,' you would never have condemned the innocent.
verses.12:8: For the Son of Man is the Lord even of the Sabbath."
verses.12:9: And when He had moved on from there, He came into their synagogue.
verses.12:10: And look, a man was there who had a withered hand; and they questioned Him, saying, "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?" so that they might accuse Him.
verses.12:11: But He said to them, "What man will there be among you who has one sheep, and if it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will he not take hold of it and lift it up?
verses.12:12: How much better indeed is a man than a sheep? Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath."
verses.12:13: Then He said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." And he stretched it out, and it was restored to health like the other.
verses.12:14: Now going out, the Pharisees were taking counsel against Him as to how they might destroy Him.
verses.12:15: But Jesus, knowing this, withdrew from there; and many followed Him, and He healed all of them,
verses.12:16: and He ordered them not to make Him known,
verses.12:17: so that what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled, saying:
verses.12:18: "Here is My servant, whom I have chosen, My beloved, in whom My soul is well pleased. I will place My Spirit upon Him, and He will announce judgment to the nations.
verses.12:19: He will not contend, nor cry out, nor will anyone hear His voice in the streets;
verses.12:20: a crushed reed He will not break, and smoldering flax He will not extinguish, until He brings forth judgment to victory;
verses.12:21: and in His name the nations will hope."
verses.12:22: Then a man who had a demon, blind and mute, was brought to Him, and He healed him, so that he spoke and saw.
verses.12:23: And all the crowds were amazed and were saying, "Could this man be the Son of David?"
verses.12:24: But the Pharisees, hearing this, said, "This man does not cast out demons except by Beelzebub, the ruler of the demons."
verses.12:25: And Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said to them, "Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.
verses.12:26: And if Satan casts out Satan, he has become divided against himself; how, therefore, will his kingdom stand?
verses.12:27: And if I cast out demons by Beelzebub, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they themselves will be your judges.
verses.12:28: But if I, by the Spirit of God, cast out demons, then the kingdom of God has reached you.
verses.12:29: Or how can anyone enter into the house of a strong man and plunder his belongings, unless he first binds the strong man? And then he will plunder his house.
verses.12:30: The one who is not with Me is against Me, and the one who does not gather with Me scatters.
verses.12:31: For this reason I say to you: Every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven people, but blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.
verses.12:32: And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; but the one who speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, neither in this age nor in the age to come.
verses.12:33: Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad; since by the fruit a tree is recognized.
verses.12:34: Offspring of vipers, how can you speak good things when you are evil? For from the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks.
verses.12:35: A good person brings out good things from a good treasury, and an evil person brings out evil things from an evil treasury.
verses.12:36: Now I say to you that for every idle word that people speak, they will render an account of it on the day of judgment.
verses.12:37: For from your words you will be justified, and from your words you will be condemned."
verses.12:38: Then some of the scribes and Pharisees answered Him, saying, "Teacher, we wish to see a sign from You."
verses.12:39: And answering, He said to them, "An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and a sign will not be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.
verses.12:40: For just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea monster for three days and three nights, so the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights.
verses.12:41: The men of Nineveh will rise up in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, because they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and look, something greater than Jonah is here.
verses.12:42: The Queen of the South will rise up in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and look, something greater than Solomon is here.
verses.12:43: Now when an unclean spirit has gone out from a person, it walks through dry places, seeking rest, and finds none.
verses.12:44: Then it says, 'I will return to my house from which I came out.' And coming, it finds it unoccupied, swept clean, and adorned.
verses.12:45: Then it goes and takes along with itself seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and entering, they dwell there; and the last state of that person becomes worse than the former. So it will also be for this most wicked generation."
verses.12:46: While He was still speaking to the crowds, look, His mother and brothers were standing outside, seeking to speak to Him.
verses.12:47: Now someone said to Him, "Look, Your mother and Your brothers are standing outside, seeking You."
verses.12:48: But answering the one who was speaking to Him, He said, "Who is My mother, and who are My brothers?"
verses.12:49: And stretching out His hand toward His disciples, He said, "Here are My mother and My brothers.
verses.12:50: For whoever does the will of My Father who is in heaven, that one is My brother, and sister, and mother."
verses.13:1: On that day, going out from the house, Jesus was sitting beside the sea.
verses.13:2: And many crowds were gathered to Him, so that He stepped into a boat and sat down, and the whole crowd was standing on the shore.
verses.13:3: And He spoke many things to them in parables, saying, "Look, the one who sows went out to sow.
verses.13:4: And while he was sowing, some fell beside the path, and the birds of the sky came and ate them.
verses.13:5: Others, however, fell onto rocky places, where they did not have much soil, and they immediately sprang up because they did not have depth of soil.
verses.13:6: But when the sun had risen, they were scorched, and because they did not have a root, they dried up.
verses.13:7: Still others fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked them.
verses.13:8: And others fell onto good soil and were yielding fruit: one a hundredfold, another sixtyfold, another thirtyfold.
verses.13:9: The one who has ears to hear, let him hear."
verses.13:10: And the disciples approached and said to Him, "Why do You speak to them in parables?"
verses.13:11: Answering, He said to them, "Because to you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, yet to them it has not been given.
verses.13:12: For whoever has, to him it will be given, and he will have an abundance; yet whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
verses.13:13: For this reason I speak to them in parables: because seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear, nor do they understand.
verses.13:14: And in them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled, who says, 'With hearing you will hear and will not understand, and seeing you will see and will not see.
verses.13:15: For the heart of this people has grown dull, and with their ears they have heard with difficulty, and they have closed their eyes, so that they would never see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn back, and I would heal them.'
verses.13:16: Yet blessed are your eyes, because they see, and your ears, because they hear.
verses.13:17: For amen, I tell you that many prophets and righteous ones longed to see what you see, and did not see it, and to hear what you hear, and did not hear it.
verses.13:18: You, therefore, hear the parable of the one who sows.
verses.13:19: Everyone who hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand: the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in his heart. This is the one who was sown beside the path.
verses.13:20: And the one who was sown on rocky places, this is the one who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy.
verses.13:21: Yet he has no root in himself, but is temporary; and when tribulation and persecution occur because of the word, he immediately stumbles.
verses.13:22: And the one who was sown among thorns, this is the one who hears the word, and the anxiety of this age and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
verses.13:23: But the one who was sown onto good soil, this is the one who hears the word and understands, and bears fruit and yields: one a hundredfold, another sixtyfold, and another thirtyfold."
verses.13:24: He set another parable before them, saying, "The kingdom of heaven has become like a man who sowed good seed in his field.
verses.13:25: But while people were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed weeds in the midst of the wheat, and went away.
verses.13:26: And when the blade had grown and had produced fruit, then the weeds also appeared.
verses.13:27: Then the servants of the master of the household came up and said to him, 'Master, did you not sow good seed in your field? From where, then, does it have weeds?'
verses.13:28: And he said to them, 'An enemy has done this.' Then the servants said to him, 'Do you want us to go and gather them?'
verses.13:29: And he said, 'No, for fear that while gathering the weeds you might uproot the wheat along with them as well.
verses.13:30: Let both grow until the harvest, and at the time of harvest I will say to the harvesters, "Gather the weeds first and bind them into bundles for burning, yet gather the wheat together into my granary."'"
verses.13:31: He set another parable before them, saying, "The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his field.
verses.13:32: It is indeed the smallest of all seeds, yet when it has grown, it is larger than all garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the sky come and dwell in its branches."
verses.13:33: He spoke another parable to them: "The kingdom of heaven is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until all of it was leavened."
verses.13:34: Jesus spoke all these things in parables to the crowds, and without parables He would not speak to them,
verses.13:35: so that what had been spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying, "I will open My mouth in parables; I will pour forth things hidden since the foundation of the world."
verses.13:36: Then, having dismissed the crowds, He came into the house, and His disciples came up to Him, saying, "Explain to us the parable of the weeds of the field."
verses.13:37: Answering, He said to them, "The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man.
verses.13:38: And the field is the world; the good seed, these are the sons of the kingdom; and the weeds are the sons of the wicked one.
verses.13:39: And the enemy who sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the age; and the harvesters are angels.
verses.13:40: Therefore, just as the weeds are gathered and burned with fire, so it will be at the end of the age.
verses.13:41: The Son of Man will send His angels, and they will gather out of His kingdom all causes of stumbling and those who commit iniquity,
verses.13:42: and they will throw them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
verses.13:43: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. The one who has ears to hear, let him hear.
verses.13:44: The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and hid; and for joy over it he goes and sells everything that he has, and buys that field.
verses.13:45: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a man who is a merchant, seeking good pearls.
verses.13:46: And having found one precious pearl, he went away and sold all that he had, and bought it.
verses.13:47: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a dragnet thrown into the sea and gathering from every kind of fish.
verses.13:48: When it was full, pulling it out and sitting beside the shore, they picked out the good ones into containers, yet the bad ones they threw out.
verses.13:49: So it will be at the end of the age: the angels will go out and separate the evil from the midst of the righteous,
verses.13:50: and they will throw them into the furnace of fire; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
verses.13:51: Have you understood all these things?" They say to Him, "Yes."
verses.13:52: He said to them, "Therefore every scribe instructed in the kingdom of heaven is like a man who is master of a household, who brings out from his treasury new things and old."
verses.13:53: And it happened that when Jesus had finished these parables, He departed from there.
verses.13:54: And coming into His own homeland, He was teaching them in their synagogues, so that they were astonished and said, "From where does this man have this wisdom and mighty works?
verses.13:55: Is He not the carpenter's son? Is not His mother called Mary, and His brothers James, and Joseph, and Simon, and Judas?
verses.13:56: And His sisters, are they not all with us? From where, then, does this Man have all these things?"
verses.13:57: And they were taking offense at Him. But Jesus said to them, "A prophet is not without honor except in his own homeland and in his own house."
verses.13:58: And He did not do many mighty works there because of their unbelief.
verses.14:1: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the report about Jesus,
verses.14:2: and said to his servants, "This is John the Baptist; he himself has risen from the dead, and for this reason powers are working in him."
verses.14:3: For Herod had seized John and bound him and put him into prison on account of Herodias, his brother's wife.
verses.14:4: For John was saying to him, "It is not permitted for you to have her."
verses.14:5: And wanting to kill him, he feared the people, because they regarded him as a prophet.
verses.14:6: Now on Herod's birthday, the daughter of Herodias danced in the center and pleased Herod;
verses.14:7: therefore with an oath he promised to give her whatever she might ask from him.
verses.14:8: But she, having been instructed beforehand by her mother, said, "Give to me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist."
verses.14:9: And the king was saddened; yet on account of the oath and those who were reclining together, he commanded that it be given.
verses.14:10: And he sent and beheaded John in prison.
verses.14:11: And his head was brought on a platter, and it was given to the young girl, and she brought it to her mother.
verses.14:12: And his disciples approached, took his body, and buried it, and came and reported it to Jesus.
verses.14:13: When Jesus had heard this, He withdrew from there in a boat to a deserted place by Himself; and when the crowds had heard, they followed Him on foot from the cities.
verses.14:14: And going out, He saw a large crowd, and had compassion on them, and healed their sick.
verses.14:15: Now when evening had come, His disciples approached Him, saying, "The place is deserted, and the hour has already passed; send the crowds away, so that going into the villages they may buy food for themselves."
verses.14:16: But Jesus said to them, "They have no need to go; you yourselves give them something to eat."
verses.14:17: They answered Him, "We have nothing here except five loaves and two fish."
verses.14:18: And He said to them, "Bring them to Me here."
verses.14:19: And when He had commanded the crowd to recline on the grass, having taken the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven, He gave a blessing, and broke and gave the loaves to the disciples, and the disciples to the crowds.
verses.14:20: And they all ate and were satisfied. And they took up the leftovers, twelve baskets full of broken pieces.
verses.14:21: Now the number of those who ate was five thousand men, excluding women and little children.
verses.14:22: And immediately Jesus compelled the disciples to board the boat and to go ahead of Him across the water while He sent the crowds away.
verses.14:23: And having sent the crowd away, He went up on the mountain alone to pray. Now when evening had come, He was there alone,
verses.14:24: but the boat was being tossed by the waves in the middle of the sea, for the wind was contrary.
verses.14:25: For in the fourth watch of the night, He came to them walking on the sea.
verses.14:26: And seeing Him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, "It is a phantom!" And because of fear they cried out.
verses.14:27: And immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying, "Have confidence; it is I, do not be afraid."
verses.14:28: And answering, Peter said, "Lord, if it is You, command me to come to You on the waters."
verses.14:29: And He said, "Come." And Peter, stepping down from the boat, was walking on the water in order to come to Jesus.
verses.14:30: But seeing the strong wind, he became afraid; and when he had begun to sink, he cried out, saying, "Lord, save me!"
verses.14:31: And at once Jesus, stretching out His hand, caught hold of him and said to him, "You of little faith, why did you doubt?"
verses.14:32: And when they had boarded the boat, the wind ceased.
verses.14:33: And those who were in the boat came and worshiped Him, saying, "Truly You are the Son of God."
verses.14:34: And when they had crossed over, they came into the land of Gennesar.
verses.14:35: And when the men of that place had recognized Him, they sent word into that entire region and brought to Him all who were ill,
verses.14:36: and they kept begging Him that they might touch even the fringe of His garment. And all who touched it were made well.
verses.15:1: Then scribes and Pharisees from Jerusalem approached Him, saying,
verses.15:2: "Why do Your disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread."
verses.15:3: But He answered and said to them, "Why do you also transgress the commandment of God because of your tradition? For God said,
verses.15:4: 'Honor father and mother,' and, 'He who curses father or mother must certainly die.'
verses.15:5: But you say, 'Whoever says to father or mother, "Whatever gift is from me will benefit you,"
verses.15:6: and he will not honor his father or his mother.' And you have nullified the commandment of God because of your tradition.
verses.15:7: Hypocrites! Isaiah prophesied well concerning you, saying,
verses.15:8: 'This people honors Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me.
verses.15:9: Yet they worship Me in vain, teaching the doctrines and commandments of men.'"
verses.15:10: And having summoned the crowds to Himself, He said to them, "Listen and understand.
verses.15:11: What enters into the mouth does not defile a man; rather, what comes forth from the mouth, this defiles a man."
verses.15:12: Then His disciples approached and said to Him, "Do You know that the Pharisees took offense when they heard this saying?"
verses.15:13: But He answered and said, "Every planting that My heavenly Father did not plant will be uprooted.
verses.15:14: Leave them alone; they are blind, and guides of the blind. And if a blind man guides a blind man, both fall into a pit."
verses.15:15: But Peter answered and said to Him, "Explain this parable to us."
verses.15:16: And He said, "Are you also still without understanding?
verses.15:17: Do you not understand that everything that enters into the mouth goes into the stomach and is discharged into the latrine?
verses.15:18: But the things that come forth from the mouth come out from the heart, and those defile a man.
verses.15:19: For from the heart come out evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false testimonies, blasphemies.
verses.15:20: These are the things that defile a man. But to eat with unwashed hands does not defile a man."
verses.15:21: And going out from there, Jesus withdrew into the districts of Tyre and Sidon.
verses.15:22: And look, a Canaanite woman, coming out from those borders, cried out, saying to Him, "Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! My daughter is severely tormented by a demon."
verses.15:23: But He did not answer her a word. And His disciples approached and were asking Him, saying, "Send her away, because she is crying out after us."
verses.15:24: But He answered and said, "I have been sent only to the sheep of the house of Israel that have been lost."
verses.15:25: Yet she came and worshiped Him, saying, "Lord, help me."
verses.15:26: And He answered and said, "It is not good to take the bread of the children and throw it to the dogs."
verses.15:27: But she said, "Yes, Lord; for even the puppies eat from the crumbs that fall from the table of their masters."
verses.15:28: Then Jesus answered and said to her, "Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish." And her daughter was healed from that hour.
verses.15:29: And when Jesus had moved on from there, He came beside the Sea of Galilee; and going up onto the mountain, He was sitting there.
verses.15:30: And great crowds approached Him, having with them the mute, the blind, the lame, the crippled, and many others; and they laid them down at His feet, and He healed them,
verses.15:31: so that the crowds were amazed as they saw the mute speaking, the lame walking, and the blind seeing; and they magnified the God of Israel.
verses.15:32: Then Jesus, having summoned His disciples, said, "I have compassion on the crowd, because for three days now they have remained with Me and have nothing to eat; and I do not wish to send them away fasting, so that they do not faint on the way."
verses.15:33: And the disciples said to Him, "Where then can we get so many loaves in the wilderness to satisfy so great a crowd?"
verses.15:34: And Jesus said to them, "How many loaves do you have?" And they said, "Seven, and a few small fish."
verses.15:35: And He commanded the crowd to recline on the ground.
verses.15:36: And taking the seven loaves and the fish, and giving thanks, He broke them and gave them to His disciples, and the disciples gave them to the people.
verses.15:37: And they all ate and were satisfied. And they picked up what was left over of the fragments, seven large baskets full.
verses.15:38: Now those who ate were four thousand men, besides little children and women.
verses.15:39: And having sent the crowd away, He boarded a boat and came into the borders of Magadan.
verses.16:1: And the Pharisees and Sadducees approached Him, testing Him, and asked Him to show them a sign from heaven.
verses.16:2: But He answered and said to them, "When evening comes, you say, 'It will be fair weather, for the sky is red.'
verses.16:3: And in the morning, 'A storm today, for the gloomy sky glows red.'
verses.16:4: So you know how to discern the face of the sky, yet can you not know the signs of the times? An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet." And having left them, He departed.
verses.16:5: And when His disciples had come across the water, they forgot to take loaves.
verses.16:6: And He said to them, "Watch closely and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees."
verses.16:7: But they were reasoning among themselves, saying, "Because we did not take loaves."
verses.16:8: But Jesus, knowing this, said, "Why are you reasoning among yourselves, you of little faith, because you have no loaves?
verses.16:9: Do you not yet understand, nor remember the five loaves for the five thousand men, and how many wicker baskets you took up?
verses.16:10: Nor the seven loaves for the four thousand men, and how many large baskets you took up?
verses.16:11: Why do you not understand that it was not about bread that I said to you, 'Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees'?"
verses.16:12: Then they understood that He had not said to beware of the leaven of loaves, but of the doctrine of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
verses.16:13: Now Jesus came into the districts of Caesarea Philippi, and He was asking His disciples, saying, "Who do people say the Son of Man is?"
verses.16:14: And they said, "Some, John the Baptist; others, Elijah; and still others, Jeremiah, or one of the prophets."
verses.16:15: Jesus said to them, "But you, who do you say that I am?"
verses.16:16: Answering, Simon Peter said, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God."
verses.16:17: And Jesus answered and said to him, "Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, because flesh and blood did not reveal this to you, but My Father who is in heaven.
verses.16:18: And I say to you that you are Peter, and upon this rock I will build My church, and the gates of the underworld will not prevail against it.
verses.16:19: And to you I will give the keys of the kingdom of heaven. And whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven also, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven also."
verses.16:20: Then He commanded His disciples to tell no one that He was Jesus Christ.
verses.16:21: From that time on, Jesus began to show His disciples that He must go to Jerusalem, and suffer many things from the elders and scribes and chief priests, and be killed, and rise again on the third day.
verses.16:22: And Peter, taking Him aside, began to rebuke Him, saying, "Far be it from You, Lord! This will not happen to You."
verses.16:23: But He turned around and said to Peter, "Get behind Me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to Me, because you do not have a mind for the things that are of God, but for those that are of men."
verses.16:24: Then Jesus said to His disciples, "If anyone desires to come after Me, let him renounce himself, and take up his cross, and follow Me.
verses.16:25: For whoever desires to save his life will lose it; yet whoever loses his life on account of Me will find it.
verses.16:26: For what does it benefit a man if he gains the entire world, yet suffers the loss of his own soul? Or what exchange will a man give for his soul?
verses.16:27: For the Son of Man is going to come in the glory of His Father with His angels, and then He will repay each one according to his works.
verses.16:28: Amen, I tell you, there are some among those standing here who will not taste death until they see the Son of Man coming in His kingdom."
verses.17:1: And after six days, Jesus took Peter and James and his brother John, and led them onto a high mountain by themselves,
verses.17:2: and He was transfigured before them. And His face shone brightly like the sun, and His garments became white like snow.
verses.17:3: And look, Moses and Elijah appeared to them, speaking with Him.
verses.17:4: Then Peter answered and said to Jesus, "Lord, it is good for us to be here. If You wish, let us make three tents: one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
verses.17:5: While he was still speaking, look, a bright cloud overshadowed them. And look, a voice came out of the cloud, saying, "This is My beloved Son, in whom I have been well pleased; listen to Him."
verses.17:6: And when the disciples heard this, they fell on their faces and were greatly afraid.
verses.17:7: And Jesus approached and touched them, and said to them, "Rise up, and do not be afraid."
verses.17:8: And lifting up their eyes, they saw no one except Jesus alone.
verses.17:9: And as they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying, "Do not tell anyone the vision until the Son of Man rises from the dead."
verses.17:10: And the disciples questioned Him, saying, "Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?"
verses.17:11: And He answered and said to them, "Elijah is indeed going to come and will restore all things.
verses.17:12: But I say to you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wished. So also the Son of Man is going to suffer from them."
verses.17:13: Then the disciples understood that He had spoken to them about John the Baptist.
verses.17:14: And when He had come to the crowd, a man approached Him, falling to his knees before Him,
verses.17:15: saying, "Lord, have mercy on my son, because he is moonstruck and suffers severely; for he often falls into the fire and frequently into the water.
verses.17:16: And I brought him to Your disciples, and they were not able to cure him."
verses.17:17: Then Jesus answered and said, "Unbelieving and perverse generation, how long will I be with you? How long will I bear with you? Bring him here to Me."
verses.17:18: And Jesus rebuked him, and the demon went out from him, and the boy was cured from that hour.
verses.17:19: Then the disciples approached Jesus privately and said, "Why were we not able to cast him out?"
verses.17:20: Jesus said to them, "Because of your unbelief. For amen, I tell you, if you have faith like a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, 'Move from here to there,' and it will move, and nothing will be impossible for you."
verses.17:22: While they were staying in Galilee, Jesus said to them, "The Son of Man is to be delivered into the hands of men,
verses.17:23: and they will kill Him, and on the third day He will rise." And they were deeply grieved.
verses.17:24: And when they had come to Capernaum, those who collected the two-drachma tax approached Peter and said to him, "Does your Teacher not pay the two-drachma tax?"
verses.17:25: He said, "Yes." And when he had entered the house, Jesus spoke to him first, saying, "What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth collect tribute or poll tax? From their own sons, or from strangers?"
verses.17:26: And he said, "From strangers." Jesus said to him, "Then the sons are free.
verses.17:27: Yet so that we do not cause them to stumble, go to the sea and cast a hook, and take the fish that comes up first; and opening its mouth, you will find a stater. Taking it, give it to them for Me and you."
verses.18:1: In that hour the disciples approached Jesus, saying, "Who, do You think, is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?"
verses.18:2: And calling a little child to Himself, Jesus set him in their midst,
verses.18:3: and said, "Amen, I tell you, unless you turn around and become like little children, you will not enter into the kingdom of heaven.
verses.18:4: Therefore, whoever humbles himself like this little child, this one is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
verses.18:5: And whoever receives one such little child in My name receives Me;
verses.18:6: but whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it is better for him that a donkey's millstone be hung around his neck and that he be sunk into the depth of the sea.
verses.18:7: Woe to the world because of stumbling blocks! For it is necessary that stumbling blocks come; nevertheless, woe to that man through whom the stumbling block comes.
verses.18:8: Now if your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter into life crippled or lame than, having two hands or two feet, to be thrown into eternal fire.
verses.18:9: And if your eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and throw it away from you. It is better for you to enter into life with one eye than, having two eyes, to be thrown into the Gehenna of fire.
verses.18:10: See that you do not despise one of these little ones; for I say to you that their angels in heaven always see the face of My Father who is in heaven.
verses.18:12: What do you think? If someone has one hundred sheep, and one of them goes astray, does he not leave the ninety-nine on the mountains and go to search for the one that went astray?
verses.18:13: And if it happens that he finds it, amen, I tell you that he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray.
verses.18:14: So it is not the will before your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.
verses.18:15: Now if your brother sins against you, go and reprove him between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you will have gained your brother.
verses.18:16: But if he does not listen to you, take with you one or two more, so that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may stand.
verses.18:17: And if he does not listen to them, tell the church. Yet if he does not listen to the church, let him be to you like a Gentile and a tax collector.
verses.18:18: Amen, I tell you, whatever you bind upon the earth will also be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose upon the earth will also be loosed in heaven.
verses.18:19: Again I say to you that if two of you agree upon the earth concerning any matter whatever they ask, it will be done for them by My Father who is in heaven.
verses.18:20: For where two or three are gathered together in My name, there I am in their midst."
verses.18:21: Then Peter, approaching Him, said, "Lord, how many times will my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Up to seven times?"
verses.18:22: Jesus said to him, "I do not say to you up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven.
verses.18:23: For this reason, the kingdom of heaven has been likened to a human king who wished to settle accounts with his servants.
verses.18:24: And when he had begun to settle accounts, one was brought to him who owed him ten thousand talents.
verses.18:25: But since he had nothing with which to repay, his master ordered him to be sold, and his wife, and children, and all that he had, and repayment to be made.
verses.18:26: Then that servant, falling down, implored him, saying, 'Have patience with me, and I will repay you everything.'
verses.18:27: And the master of that servant, taking pity, released him and forgave him the debt.
verses.18:28: But going out, that servant found one of his fellow servants who owed him one hundred denarii; and seizing him, he choked him, saying, 'Repay what you owe.'
verses.18:29: And falling down, his fellow servant pleaded with him, saying, 'Have patience with me, and I will repay you everything.'
