verses.18:30: But he was unwilling; instead he went away and threw him into prison until he repaid the debt.
verses.18:31: Now when his fellow servants saw what was happening, they were greatly grieved, and they came and reported to their master everything that had happened.
verses.18:32: Then his master summoned him and said to him, 'Wicked servant, I forgave you the entire debt because you pleaded with me;
verses.18:33: should you not therefore also have had pity on your fellow servant, just as I also had pity on you?'
verses.18:34: And his master, being angry, handed him over to the torturers until he repaid the whole debt.
verses.18:35: So also will My heavenly Father do to you, if each of you does not forgive his brother from your hearts."
verses.19:1: And it happened that, when Jesus had completed these discourses, He departed from Galilee and came into the borders of Judea across the Jordan,
verses.19:2: and large crowds followed Him, and He healed them there.
verses.19:3: And Pharisees approached Him, testing Him and saying, "Is it lawful for a man to send away his wife for any cause whatever?"
verses.19:4: Answering, He said to them, "Have you not read that He who made man from the beginning made them male and female? And He said,
verses.19:5: 'For this reason a man will leave father and mother and cling to his wife, and the two will be in one flesh.'
verses.19:6: Consequently, they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore, what God has joined together, man must not separate."
verses.19:7: They said to Him, "Why then did Moses command one to give a certificate of divorce and send her away?"
verses.19:8: He said to them, "Because Moses, on account of the hardness of your heart, permitted you to send away your wives; from the beginning, however, it was not like this.
verses.19:9: Now I tell you that whoever sends away his wife, except on account of fornication, and marries another commits adultery; and the one who marries a woman who has been sent away commits adultery."
verses.19:10: His disciples said to Him, "If the case of a man with a wife is like this, it is not advantageous to marry."
verses.19:11: He said to them, "Not all receive this word, but those to whom it has been given.
verses.19:12: For there are eunuchs who were born that way from their mother's womb; and there are eunuchs who were made so by men; and there are eunuchs who have castrated themselves for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Whoever can receive it, let him receive it."
verses.19:13: Then little children were brought to Him, so that He might lay hands on them and pray. But the disciples were rebuking them.
verses.19:14: But Jesus said to them, "Leave the little children alone, and do not prevent them from coming to Me, for it is to such as these that the kingdom of heaven belongs."
verses.19:15: And when He had laid hands on them, He went away from there.
verses.19:16: And look, someone approached and said to Him, "Good Teacher, what good thing should I do so that I may have eternal life?"
verses.19:17: He said to him, "Why do you question Me about what is good? One is good: God. Now if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments."
verses.19:18: He said to Him, "Which ones?" And Jesus said, "You shall not commit murder; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not commit theft; you shall not give false testimony;
verses.19:19: honor your father and your mother; and you shall love your neighbor as yourself."
verses.19:20: The young man said to Him, "All these things I have observed from my youth; what do I still lack?"
verses.19:21: Jesus said to him, "If you want to be perfect, go, sell what you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow Me."
verses.19:22: Now when the young man had heard the word, he went away sorrowful, for he had many possessions.
verses.19:23: And Jesus said to His disciples, "Amen, I tell you that a rich man will enter the kingdom of heaven with difficulty.
verses.19:24: And again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to pass through a needle's eye than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven."
verses.19:25: Now on hearing these things, the disciples were greatly amazed, saying, "Who, then, will be able to be saved?"
verses.19:26: Looking at them, Jesus said to them, "With human beings this is impossible; with God, however, everything is possible."
verses.19:27: Then, answering, Peter said to Him, "Look, we have left everything and followed You; what then will there be for us?"
verses.19:28: And Jesus said to them, "Amen, I tell you that you who have followed Me, in the regeneration, when the Son of Man sits on the throne of His majesty, you also will sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
verses.19:29: And everyone who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or fields for the sake of My name will receive a hundredfold and will possess eternal life.
verses.19:30: However, many who are first will be last, and the last will be first."
verses.20:1: "The kingdom of heaven is like a man, the master of a household, who went out early in the morning to hire laborers for his vineyard.
verses.20:2: And when an agreement had been made with the laborers for a denarius a day, he sent them into his vineyard.
verses.20:3: And going out about the third hour, he saw others standing idle in the marketplace,
verses.20:4: and he said to them, 'You also go into my vineyard, and I will give you what is just.'
verses.20:5: And they went away. Again he went out about the sixth and the ninth hour, and did likewise.
verses.20:6: Then about the eleventh hour he went out and found others standing, and said to them, 'Why are you standing here idle all day?'
verses.20:7: They said to him, 'Because no one has hired us.' He said to them, 'You also go into my vineyard.'
verses.20:8: Now when evening had come, the owner of the vineyard said to his steward, 'Call the laborers and pay them their wages, beginning from the last up to the first.'
verses.20:9: So when those who had come about the eleventh hour arrived, they each received a denarius.
verses.20:10: And when the first ones also came, they supposed that they were going to receive more; yet they themselves also each received a denarius.
verses.20:11: And upon receiving it, they were grumbling against the master of the household,
verses.20:12: saying, 'These last ones worked one hour, and you have made them equal to us, who have borne the weight of the day and the heat.'
verses.20:13: But answering one of them, he said, 'Friend, I am doing you no wrong; did you not agree with me for a denarius?
verses.20:14: Take what is yours and go; yet I wish to give to this last one also, just as to you.
verses.20:15: Or is it not lawful for me to do what I wish? Or is your eye evil because I am good?'
verses.20:16: In this way, the last will be first, and the first, last. For many are called, yet few are chosen."
verses.20:17: And as Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, He took the twelve disciples privately and said to them,
verses.20:18: "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes, and they will condemn Him to death,
verses.20:19: and will hand Him over to the Gentiles to be mocked, and flogged, and crucified, and on the third day He will rise again."
verses.20:20: Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee approached Him with her sons, worshiping and asking something from Him.
verses.20:21: He said to her, "What do you want?" She said to Him, "Say that these two sons of mine may sit, one at Your right and one at Your left, in Your kingdom."
verses.20:22: But Jesus answered and said, "You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink?" They said to Him, "We are able."
verses.20:23: He said to them, "My cup indeed you will drink; but to sit at My right or left is not Mine to give to you; rather, it is for those for whom it has been prepared by My Father."
verses.20:24: And when the ten heard this, they were indignant about the two brothers.
verses.20:25: But Jesus called them to Himself and said, "You know that the rulers of the Gentiles exercise dominion over them, and those who are greater exercise authority over them.
verses.20:26: It will not be like this among you; rather, whoever wants to become greater among you, let him be your servant,
verses.20:27: and whoever wants to be first among you will be your slave,
verses.20:28: just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a redemption for many."
verses.20:29: And as they were going out from Jericho, a large crowd followed Him,
verses.20:30: and look, two blind men sitting beside the road heard that Jesus was passing by, and they cried out, saying, "Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David."
verses.20:31: Now the crowd was rebuking them so that they would keep silent. Yet they kept crying out all the more, saying, "Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David."
verses.20:32: And Jesus stopped and called them, and said, "What do you want Me to do for you?"
verses.20:33: They said to Him, "Lord, that our eyes may be opened."
verses.20:34: And moved with compassion for them, Jesus touched their eyes. And immediately they saw, and followed Him.
verses.21:1: And when they had drawn near to Jerusalem and had come to Bethphage at the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,
verses.21:2: saying to them, "Go into the village that lies opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied up, and a colt with her; untie them and bring them to Me.
verses.21:3: And if anyone says anything to you, say, 'The Lord has need of these,' and at once he will let them go."
verses.21:4: Now all this happened so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying,
verses.21:5: "Say to the daughter of Zion, 'Look, your king is coming to you, gentle, sitting upon a donkey, and a colt, the foal of a beast under the yoke.'"
verses.21:6: Now the disciples went and did as Jesus had commanded them.
verses.21:7: And they brought the donkey and the colt, and placed their garments on them, and had Him sit on top.
verses.21:8: Now a very great crowd spread their garments on the road, while others were cutting branches from the trees and spreading them on the road.
verses.21:9: And the crowds that were going ahead and that were following were crying out, saying, "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!"
verses.21:10: And when He had entered Jerusalem, the entire city was thrown into commotion, saying, "Who is this?"
verses.21:11: And the people were saying, "This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth of Galilee."
verses.21:12: And Jesus entered the temple of God and was driving out all those selling and buying in the temple, and He overturned the tables of the moneychangers and the seats of those selling doves.
verses.21:13: And He said to them, "It is written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer,' but you have made it a cave of robbers."
verses.21:14: And the blind and the lame approached Him in the temple, and He healed them.
verses.21:15: But when the chief priests and the scribes saw the marvelous things that He did, and the children crying out in the temple and saying, "Hosanna to the Son of David!" they became indignant,
verses.21:16: and said to Him, "Do You hear what these are saying?" And Jesus said to them, "Yes. Have you never read, 'From the mouth of infants and those who are nursing You have perfected praise'?"
verses.21:17: And leaving them, He went out beyond the city to Bethany and stayed there.
verses.21:18: Now in the morning, returning into the city, He grew hungry.
verses.21:19: And seeing a single fig tree beside the road, He came to it and found nothing on it except leaves alone, and He said to it, "May fruit never grow from you forever." And instantly the fig tree dried up.
verses.21:20: And seeing it, the disciples marveled, saying, "How did it dry up instantly?"
verses.21:21: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Amen, I tell you, if you have faith and do not hesitate, you will not only do what happened to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, 'Lift yourself up and throw yourself into the sea,' it will be done.
verses.21:22: And all things, whatever you ask in prayer, believing, you will receive."
verses.21:23: And when He had come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people approached Him as He was teaching, saying, "By what authority do You do these things? And who gave You this authority?"
verses.21:24: Answering, Jesus said to them, "I too will ask you one thing; if you tell it to Me, I too will tell you by what authority I do these things.
verses.21:25: Where was the baptism of John from? From heaven, or from men?" But they were reasoning among themselves, saying,
verses.21:26: "If we say, 'From heaven,' He will say to us, 'Why then did you not believe him?' But if we say, 'From men,' we fear the crowd, for all regarded John as a prophet."
verses.21:27: And answering Jesus, they said, "We do not know." He Himself also said to them, "Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
verses.21:28: Now what do you think? A certain man had two sons, and approaching the first, he said, 'Son, go today, work in my vineyard.'
verses.21:29: But he answered and said, 'I will not.' Afterward, however, moved by repentance, he went.
verses.21:30: And approaching the other, he spoke in the same way. But he answered and said, 'I am going, sir,' and he did not go.
verses.21:31: Which of the two did the will of the father?" They said to Him, "The first." Jesus said to them, "Amen, I tell you that tax collectors and prostitutes will go ahead of you into the kingdom of God.
verses.21:32: For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him, whereas tax collectors and prostitutes believed him; and you, seeing this, did not even repent afterward so as to believe him.
verses.21:33: Hear another parable: There was a man, a householder, who planted a vineyard, and put a hedge around it, and dug a winepress in it, and built a tower, and leased it to farmers, and departed abroad.
verses.21:34: Now when the time of the fruits had drawn near, he sent his servants to the farmers so that they might receive its fruits.
verses.21:35: And the farmers, having seized his servants, beat one, killed another, and stoned still another.
verses.21:36: Again he sent other servants, more than the earlier ones, and they did to them in the same way.
verses.21:37: And last of all he sent his son to them, saying, 'They will respect my son.'
verses.21:38: But the farmers, seeing the son, said among themselves, 'This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and we will have his inheritance.'
verses.21:39: And seizing him, they threw him outside the vineyard and killed him.
verses.21:40: Therefore, when the master of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers?"
verses.21:41: They said to Him, "He will miserably destroy those wicked men and will lease his vineyard to other farmers, who will deliver the fruit to him in its seasons."
verses.21:42: Jesus said to them, "Have you never read in the Scriptures, 'The stone that the builders rejected, this one has been made the head of the corner; by the Lord this was done, and it is marvelous in our eyes'?
verses.21:43: Therefore I say to you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a nation producing its fruits.
verses.21:44: And the one who falls on this stone will be shattered; but on whomever it falls, it will crush him."
verses.21:45: And when the chief priests and the Pharisees had heard His parables, they realized that He was speaking about them.
verses.21:46: And while seeking to lay hold of Him, they feared the crowds, because they regarded Him as a prophet.
verses.22:1: And answering, Jesus spoke to them again in parables, saying,
verses.22:2: "The kingdom of heaven has become like a man who was a king, who held a wedding feast for his son.
verses.22:3: And he sent his servants to call those who had been invited to the wedding feast, and they did not want to come.
verses.22:4: Again he sent other servants, saying, 'Tell those who have been invited, "Look, I have prepared my dinner; my bulls and fattened animals have been slaughtered, and everything is ready; come to the wedding feast."'
verses.22:5: But they disregarded it and went away, one to his farm and another to his business,
verses.22:6: while the rest laid hold of his servants, subjected them to abuse, and killed them.
verses.22:7: Now when the king heard this, he grew angry; and having sent his armies, he destroyed those murderers and set fire to their city.
verses.22:8: Then he said to his servants, 'The wedding feast is indeed ready, but those who had been invited were not worthy.
verses.22:9: Go therefore to the outlets of the roads, and whoever you find, call to the wedding feast.'
verses.22:10: And his servants went out into the roads and gathered together all whom they found, bad and good; and the wedding feast was filled with those reclining at table.
verses.22:11: Now the king entered to see those reclining at table, and he saw there a man not clothed in a wedding garment.
verses.22:12: And he said to him, 'Friend, how did you enter here without having a wedding garment?' But he fell silent.
verses.22:13: Then the king said to the attendants, 'Bind his hands and feet and cast him into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.'
verses.22:14: For many are called, yet few are chosen."
verses.22:15: Then going away, the Pharisees took counsel so that they might catch Him in speech.
verses.22:16: And they sent their disciples to Him with the Herodians, saying, "Teacher, we know that You are truthful and teach the way of God in truth, and You are not concerned about anyone, for You do not look to the person of men;
verses.22:17: tell us therefore what You think: is it lawful to pay the census tax to Caesar, or not?"
verses.22:18: But Jesus, recognizing their wickedness, said, "Why are you testing Me, hypocrites?
verses.22:19: Show Me the coin of the census tax." Then they presented a denarius to Him.
verses.22:20: And Jesus said to them, "Whose is this image and inscription?"
verses.22:21: They said to Him, "Caesar's." Then He said to them, "Give back therefore what is Caesar's to Caesar, and what is God's to God."
verses.22:22: When they heard this, they marveled, and having left Him, they went away.
verses.22:23: On that day, Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection, approached Him and questioned Him,
verses.22:24: saying, "Teacher, Moses said that if anyone dies without having a son, his brother should marry his wife and raise up seed for his brother.
verses.22:25: Now there were seven brothers among us; and the first, having taken a wife, died, and having no seed, left his wife to his brother.
verses.22:26: Similarly, the second and the third, all the way to the seventh.
verses.22:27: And last of all, the woman died as well.
verses.22:28: In the resurrection, therefore, whose wife among the seven will she be? For they all had her."
verses.22:29: But answering, Jesus said to them, "You are in error, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God.
verses.22:30: For in the resurrection they will neither marry nor be married, but will be like the angels of God in heaven.
verses.22:31: Now concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what was spoken by God, saying to you,
verses.22:32: 'I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob'? He is not a God of the dead, but of the living."
verses.22:33: And hearing this, the crowds were marveling at His teaching.
verses.22:34: Now when the Pharisees heard that He had imposed silence on the Sadducees, they came together as one,
verses.22:35: and one of them, a teacher of the law, questioned Him, testing Him,
verses.22:36: "Teacher, what is the great commandment in the law?"
verses.22:37: Jesus said to him, "You shall love the Lord your God from your whole heart, and in your whole soul, and in your whole mind.
verses.22:38: This is the greatest and foremost commandment.
verses.22:39: And the second is like this one: 'You shall love your neighbor just as yourself.'
verses.22:40: Upon these two commandments depends the entire law, and the prophets."
verses.22:41: Now when the Pharisees had gathered together, Jesus questioned them,
verses.22:42: saying, "What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is He?" They said to Him, "David's."
verses.22:43: He said to them, "How therefore does David, in the Spirit, call Him Lord, saying,
verses.22:44: 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at My right hand, until I place Your enemies as a footstool for Your feet"'?
verses.22:45: If therefore David calls Him Lord, how is He his son?"
verses.22:46: And no one could answer Him a word, nor did anyone dare from that day forward to question Him any further.
verses.23:1: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds, and to His disciples,
verses.23:2: saying, "The scribes and the Pharisees have sat upon the seat of Moses.
verses.23:3: Therefore, observe and do all things, whatever they tell you; yet do not act according to their works, for they speak and do not act.
verses.23:4: For they bind up heavy and unbearable burdens and lay them upon the shoulders of men, yet with their own finger they are unwilling to move them.
verses.23:5: But they do all their works so that they may be seen by men; for they broaden their phylacteries and enlarge the fringes.
verses.23:6: And they love the first reclining places at banquets, and the first seats in the synagogues,
verses.23:7: and greetings in the marketplace, and to be called Rabbi by men.
verses.23:8: But you, do not be called Rabbi; for one is your Teacher, and all of you are brothers.
verses.23:9: And do not call anyone upon the earth your father; for one is your Father, who is in heaven.
verses.23:10: Nor be called teachers, because your Teacher is one, Christ.
verses.23:11: The one who is greatest among you will be your servant.
verses.23:12: Now the one who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.
verses.23:13: But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you shut the kingdom of heaven before men! For you yourselves do not enter, nor do you permit those who are entering to enter.
verses.23:15: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you go around sea and dry land so that you may make one proselyte, and when he has become one, you make him a son of Gehenna twice as much as yourselves.
verses.23:16: Woe to you, blind guides, who say, 'Whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the temple is bound.'
verses.23:17: Fools and blind ones! For which is greater? The gold, or the temple that sanctifies the gold?
verses.23:18: And, 'Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift that is upon it is bound.'
verses.23:19: Blind ones! For which is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifies the gift?
verses.23:20: Therefore, the one who swears by the altar swears by it and by all things that are upon it.
verses.23:21: And whoever swears by the temple swears by it and by Him who dwells in it;
verses.23:22: and the one who swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by Him who sits upon it.
verses.23:23: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who tithe mint, and dill, and cumin, and have left aside the weightier things of the law: judgment, and mercy, and faith! These things you ought to have done, and not to have omitted those.
verses.23:24: Blind guides, straining out a gnat, yet swallowing a camel.
verses.23:25: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you clean what is on the outside of the cup and the dish, yet inside you are full of robbery and uncleanness!
verses.23:26: Blind Pharisee, clean first what is on the inside of the cup and the dish, so that what is on the outside may become clean.
verses.23:27: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you are like whitewashed tombs, which on the outside appear beautiful to men, yet inside they are full of bones of the dead and all filth!
verses.23:28: So you also indeed appear righteous to men on the outside, yet inside you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.
verses.23:29: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, who build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the monuments of the righteous,
verses.23:30: and say, 'If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been their partners in the blood of the prophets!'
verses.23:31: Therefore, you are a witness against yourselves that you are sons of those who killed the prophets.
verses.23:32: And you, fill up the measure of your fathers.
verses.23:33: Serpents, offspring of vipers, how will you flee from the judgment of Gehenna?
verses.23:34: For this reason, look, I send to you prophets, and wise men, and scribes; and some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues and persecute from city to city,
verses.23:35: so that all the righteous blood that has been shed upon the earth may come upon you, from the blood of Abel the righteous up to the blood of Zechariah, son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the temple and the altar.
verses.23:36: Amen, I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation.
verses.23:37: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those who have been sent to you, how many times have I wanted to gather your children, just as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you were unwilling?
verses.23:38: Look, your house will be left to you desolate.
verses.23:39: For I tell you, you will not see Me from now on until you say, 'Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.'"
verses.24:1: And having gone out from the temple, Jesus was walking away. And His disciples approached to show Him the buildings of the temple.
verses.24:2: But He answered and said to them, "Do you see all these things? Amen, I tell you, not a stone will be left here upon a stone that will not be torn down."
verses.24:3: Now while He was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples approached Him privately, saying, "Tell us, when will these things be? And what will be the sign of Your coming and of the consummation of the age?"
verses.24:4: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Watch out that no one leads you astray;
verses.24:5: for many will come in My name, saying, 'I am the Christ,' and they will lead many astray.
verses.24:6: For you are going to hear of wars and reports of wars. Watch out that you are not troubled; for these things must take place, but the end is not yet;
verses.24:7: for nation will rise up against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be plagues, and famines, and earthquakes in various places;
verses.24:8: but all these things are the beginnings of pains.
verses.24:9: Then they will hand you over to tribulation and kill you, and you will be an object of hatred to all nations on account of My name.
verses.24:10: And then many will stumble, and they will hand one another over, and will hate one another.
verses.24:11: And many false prophets will rise up, and they will lead many astray.
verses.24:12: And since iniquity has abounded, the love of many will grow cold;
verses.24:13: but the one who perseveres to the end, this one will be saved.
verses.24:14: And this gospel of the kingdom will be proclaimed in the entire world as a testimony to all nations, and then the consummation will come.
verses.24:15: Therefore, when you see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of by the prophet Daniel, standing in the holy place (let the one who reads understand),
verses.24:16: then those who are in Judea, let them flee to the mountains;
verses.24:17: and the one on the roof, let him not go down to take anything from his house;
verses.24:18: and the one in the field, let him not turn back to take his tunic.
verses.24:19: But woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days!
verses.24:20: But pray that your flight may not take place in winter or on a Sabbath;
verses.24:21: for then there will be great tribulation, such as has not taken place from the beginning of the world up to now, nor will take place.
verses.24:22: And unless those days had been shortened, no flesh would be saved; but on account of the elect, those days will be shortened.
verses.24:23: Then if anyone says to you, 'Look, here is the Christ,' or 'There,' do not believe it.
verses.24:24: For false christs and false prophets will rise up, and they will give great signs and wonders, so that (if it is possible) even the elect might be led into error.
verses.24:25: Look, I have told you in advance.
verses.24:26: Therefore, if they say to you, 'Look, He is in the desert,' do not go out; 'Look, in the inner rooms,' do not believe it.
verses.24:27: For just as lightning goes out from the east and appears all the way to the west, so also will the coming of the Son of Man be.
verses.24:28: Wherever the body is, there the eagles also will be gathered.
verses.24:29: Now immediately after the tribulation of those days, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken;
verses.24:30: and then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven; and then all the tribes of the earth will lament, and they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds of heaven with great power and majesty.
verses.24:31: And He will send His angels with a trumpet and a loud voice, and they will gather His elect from the four winds, from the heights of the heavens all the way to their boundaries.
verses.24:32: Now learn a parable from the fig tree: when its branch has already become tender and leaves have sprung forth, you know that summer is near;
verses.24:33: so you also, when you see all these things, know that it is near, at the doors.
verses.24:34: Amen, I tell you that this generation will not pass away until all these things take place.
verses.24:35: Heaven and earth will pass away; My words, however, will not pass away.
verses.24:36: Now concerning that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels of the heavens, except the Father alone.
verses.24:37: Now just as in the days of Noah, so also will the coming of the Son of Man be;
verses.24:38: for just as in the days before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, up to that day on which Noah entered the ark,
verses.24:39: and they did not know until the flood came and carried them all away; so also will the coming of the Son of Man be.
verses.24:40: Then two men will be in the field: one will be taken, and one will be left behind.
verses.24:41: Two women will be grinding at the mill: one will be taken, and one will be left behind.
verses.24:42: Keep watch, therefore, because you do not know at what hour your Lord is coming.
verses.24:43: Now know this, that if the head of the household knew at what hour the thief was going to come, he would certainly keep watch and would not allow his house to be broken into.
verses.24:44: For this reason, you also be ready, because at an hour you do not know, the Son of Man is coming.
verses.24:45: Who, do you think, is the faithful and prudent servant whom his master appointed over his household to give them food at the proper time?
verses.24:46: Blessed is that servant whom his master, when he comes, will find doing so.
verses.24:47: Amen, I tell you that he will appoint him over all his possessions.
verses.24:48: But if that wicked servant says in his heart, 'My master has delayed in coming,'
verses.24:49: and begins to beat his fellow servants, and also eats and drinks with drunkards,
verses.24:50: the master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour of which he is unaware,
verses.24:51: and he will divide him and place his portion with the hypocrites; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth in that place."
verses.25:1: "Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins who, taking their lamps, went out to meet the bridegroom and the bride.
verses.25:2: Now five of them were foolish, and five prudent.
verses.25:3: But the five foolish ones, after taking their lamps, took no oil with them.
verses.25:4: The prudent ones, however, took oil in their vessels along with the lamps.
verses.25:5: While the bridegroom delayed, however, all of them grew drowsy and slept.
verses.25:6: Now at midnight a cry arose, 'Look, the bridegroom is coming; go out to meet him.'
verses.25:7: Then all of those virgins got up and trimmed their lamps.
verses.25:8: And the foolish ones said to the wise ones, 'Give us some of your oil, because our lamps are going out.'
verses.25:9: The prudent ones answered, saying, 'In case there is not enough for us and for you, go instead to those who sell, and buy for yourselves.'
verses.25:10: Now while they were going to buy, the bridegroom arrived; and the ones who were ready entered with him to the wedding, and the door was shut.
verses.25:11: Last of all the remaining virgins also came, saying, 'Lord, lord, open for us.'
verses.25:12: But answering, he said, 'Amen, I tell you, I do not know you.'
verses.25:13: Keep watch, therefore, because you do not know the day nor the hour.
verses.25:14: For it is like a man setting out on a journey abroad, who called his servants and handed over his possessions to them.
verses.25:15: And to one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one, to each according to his own ability; and he set out immediately.
verses.25:16: Now the one who had received five talents went away and worked with them, and gained another five.
verses.25:17: Likewise, the one who had received two also gained another two.
verses.25:18: But the one who had received one went away, dug into the ground, and hid his master's money.
verses.25:19: After a long time, however, the master of those servants came and settled accounts with them.
verses.25:20: And the one who had received five talents came forward and presented another five talents, saying, 'Master, you handed over five talents to me; look, I have gained another five in addition.'
verses.25:21: His master said to him, 'Well done, good and faithful servant! Because you were faithful over a few things, I will appoint you over many things; enter into the joy of your master.'
verses.25:22: Then the one who had received two talents also came forward and said, 'Master, you handed over two talents to me; look, I have gained another two.'
verses.25:23: His master said to him, 'Well done, good and faithful servant! Because you were faithful over a few things, I will appoint you over many things; enter into the joy of your master.'
verses.25:24: Then the one who had received one talent also came forward and said, 'Master, I know that you are a harsh man: you reap where you did not sow, and you gather where you did not scatter;
verses.25:25: and being afraid, I went away and hid your talent in the ground; look, you have what is yours.'
verses.25:26: But in reply his master said to him, 'Wicked and lazy servant, you knew that I reap where I do not sow and gather where I did not scatter;
verses.25:27: therefore you ought to have entrusted my money to the bankers, and when I came, I would certainly have received back what is mine with interest.
verses.25:28: Take the talent away from him, therefore, and give it to the one who has ten talents.
verses.25:29: For to everyone who has, it will be given, and he will abound; but as for the one who does not have, even what he seems to have will be taken away from him.
verses.25:30: And cast out the useless servant into the outer darkness; in that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.'
verses.25:31: Now when the Son of Man comes in His majesty, and all the angels with Him, then He will sit on the throne of His majesty.
verses.25:32: And all the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate them from one another, just as a shepherd divides the sheep from the goats;
verses.25:33: and He will set the sheep on His right, and the goats on the left.
verses.25:34: Then the King will say to those who will be on His right, 'Come, you blessed of My Father, take possession of the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world;
verses.25:35: for I was hungry, and you gave Me something to eat; I was thirsty, and you gave Me something to drink; I was a stranger, and you took Me in;
verses.25:36: naked, and you covered Me; ill, and you visited Me; I was in prison, and you came to Me.'
verses.25:37: Then the righteous will answer Him, saying, 'Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You, thirsty and give You a drink?
verses.25:38: And when did we see You a stranger and take You in, or naked and cover You?
verses.25:39: Or when did we see You ill, or in prison, and come to You?'
verses.25:40: And answering, the King will say to them, 'Amen, I tell you, as long as you did it for one of these least brothers of Mine, you did it for Me.'
verses.25:41: Then He will also say to those who will be on the left, 'Depart from Me, you cursed ones, into the eternal fire that has been prepared for the devil and his angels;
verses.25:42: for I was hungry, and you did not give Me anything to eat; I was thirsty, and you did not give Me a drink;
verses.25:43: I was a stranger, and you did not take Me in; naked, and you did not cover Me; ill and in prison, and you did not visit Me.'
verses.25:44: Then they themselves will also answer Him, saying, 'Lord, when did we see You hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or ill, or in prison, and not serve You?'
verses.25:45: Then He will answer them, saying, 'Amen, I tell you, as long as you did not do it for one of these lesser ones, neither did you do it for Me.'
verses.25:46: And these will go into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life."
verses.26:1: And it happened that when Jesus had completed all these discourses, He said to His disciples:
verses.26:2: "You know that after two days the Passover will take place, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified."
verses.26:3: Then the chief priests and the elders of the people were gathered together in the courtyard of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas,
verses.26:4: and they formed a plan to seize Jesus by deceit and kill Him.
verses.26:5: But they were saying, "Not on the festival day, in case an uproar should arise among the people."
verses.26:6: Now while Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
verses.26:7: a woman approached Him holding an alabaster jar of costly ointment, and she poured it out over His head as He reclined.
verses.26:8: But seeing this, the disciples grew indignant, saying, "For what purpose is this waste?
verses.26:9: For this could have been sold for a great deal and given to the poor."
verses.26:10: But Jesus, knowing this, said to them, "Why are you causing trouble for this woman? For she has performed a good work toward Me.
verses.26:11: For you always have the poor with you; Me, however, you do not always have.
verses.26:12: For in putting this ointment on My body, this woman did it for My burial.
verses.26:13: Amen, I tell you, wherever this Gospel is preached in the entire world, what this woman did will also be told in remembrance of her."
verses.26:14: Then one of the twelve, who was called Judas Iscariot, went off to the chief priests,
verses.26:15: and said to them, "What do you want to give me, and I will hand Him over to you?" And they assigned him thirty silver coins.
verses.26:16: And from then on he was seeking an opportunity to hand Him over.
verses.26:17: Now on the first day of Unleavened Bread, the disciples approached Jesus, saying, "Where do You wish us to prepare for You to eat the Passover?"
verses.26:18: And Jesus said, "Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, 'The Teacher says, "My time is near; at your house I am celebrating the Passover with My disciples."'"
verses.26:19: And the disciples did just as Jesus had instructed them, and they prepared the Passover.
verses.26:20: Now when evening had come, He was reclining at table with His twelve disciples.
verses.26:21: And as they were eating, He said, "Amen, I tell you that one of you is about to hand Me over."
verses.26:22: And deeply grieved, they began one by one to say, "It is not I, is it, Lord?"
verses.26:23: And He answered and said, "The one who dips his hand with Me in the dish, this one will hand Me over.
verses.26:24: The Son of Man indeed goes just as it is written about Him, yet woe to that man through whom the Son of Man will be handed over! It would have been good for him if that man had not been born."
verses.26:25: Then Judas, who handed Him over, answered and said, "It is not I, is it, Rabbi?" He said to him, "You have said it."
verses.26:26: Now while they were eating supper, Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to His disciples, and said, "Take and eat: this is My body."
verses.26:27: And taking a cup, He gave thanks and gave it to them, saying, "Drink from this, all of you.
verses.26:28: For this is My blood of the new covenant, which will be poured out on behalf of many for the forgiveness of sins.
verses.26:29: But I tell you, from now on I will not drink of this produce of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of My Father."
verses.26:30: And when a hymn had been recited, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
verses.26:31: Then Jesus said to them, "All of you will suffer stumbling because of Me on this night. For it is written, 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be dispersed.'
verses.26:32: But after I have risen again, I will go ahead of you into Galilee."
verses.26:33: But Peter answered and said to Him, "Even if all are made to stumble because of You, I will never be made to stumble."
verses.26:34: Jesus said to him, "Amen, I tell you that on this night, before a rooster crows, you will deny Me three times."
verses.26:35: Peter said to Him, "Even if it is necessary for me to die with You, I will not deny You." All the disciples also spoke in the same way.
verses.26:36: Then Jesus came with them to an estate that is called Gethsemane, and He said to His disciples, "Remain seated here while I go over there and pray."
verses.26:37: And taking along Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, He began to grow sorrowful and heavy-hearted.
verses.26:38: Then He said to them, "My soul is sorrowful to the point of death; wait here and stay awake with Me."
verses.26:39: And advancing a little farther, He fell onto His face, praying and saying, "My Father, if it is possible, may this cup pass from Me; yet not as I will, but as You do."
verses.26:40: And He came to His disciples and found them sleeping, and He said to Peter, "So were you not able to stay awake with Me for one hour?
verses.26:41: Stay awake and pray so that you do not enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is ready, yet the flesh is weak."
verses.26:42: Again, a second time, He went away and prayed, saying, "My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, may Your will be done."
verses.26:43: And He came again and found them sleeping, for their eyes were weighed down.
verses.26:44: And having left them, He went away again and prayed a third time, saying the same words.
verses.26:45: Then He came to His disciples and said to them, "Sleep now and rest; look, the hour has drawn near, and the Son of Man will be handed over into the hands of sinners.
verses.26:46: Get up, let us go; look, the one who will hand Me over has drawn near."
verses.26:47: While He was still speaking, look, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests and the elders of the people.
verses.26:48: Now the one who handed Him over gave them a sign, saying, "Whoever I kiss, He is the one; seize Him."
verses.26:49: And immediately approaching Jesus, he said, "Greetings, Rabbi." And he kissed Him.
verses.26:50: And Jesus said to him, "Friend, for what purpose have you come?" Then they approached, laid hands on Jesus, and seized Him.
verses.26:51: And look, one of those who were with Jesus, stretching out his hand, drew out his sword, and striking the servant of the high priest, cut off his ear.
verses.26:52: Then Jesus said to him, "Return your sword to its place, for all those who take the sword will perish by the sword.
verses.26:53: Or do you suppose that I cannot ask My Father, and He will provide for Me right now more than twelve legions of angels?
verses.26:54: How then will the Scriptures be fulfilled, that it must come about in this way?"
verses.26:55: In that hour Jesus said to the crowds, "You have come out as against a robber with swords and clubs to capture Me; every day I sat with you teaching in the temple, and you did not seize Me."
verses.26:56: Now all of this happened so that the Scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled. Then all the disciples, having left Him, fled.
verses.26:57: And those who had seized Jesus led Him to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders had assembled.
verses.26:58: But Peter was following Him from a distance, all the way into the courtyard of the high priest. And entering inside, he was sitting with the attendants to see the outcome.
verses.26:59: Now the chief priests and the whole council were seeking false testimony against Jesus so that they might hand Him over to death,
verses.26:60: and they found none, even though many false witnesses had come forward. Last of all, however, two false witnesses came,
verses.26:61: and said, "This man said, 'I am able to destroy the temple of God and after three days rebuild it.'"
verses.26:62: And standing up, the high priest said to Him, "Do You answer nothing to the things that these men are testifying against You?"
verses.26:63: But Jesus remained silent. And the high priest said to Him, "I put You under oath by the living God to tell us whether You are the Christ, the Son of God."
verses.26:64: Jesus said to him, "You have said it. Nevertheless, I tell you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the power of God and coming in the clouds of heaven."
verses.26:65: Then the high priest tore his garments, saying, "He has blasphemed! What further need do we have of witnesses? Look, now you have heard the blasphemy;
verses.26:66: what is your opinion?" And answering, they said, "He is deserving of death."
verses.26:67: Then they spat in His face and beat Him with their fists, while others struck His face with the palms of their hands,
verses.26:68: saying, "Prophesy to us, Christ: who is the one who struck You?"
verses.26:69: Now Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and one servant girl approached him, saying, "You too were with Jesus the Galilean."
verses.26:70: But he denied it in front of everyone, saying, "I do not know what you are saying."
verses.26:71: Now as he was going out the gateway, another servant girl saw him and said to those who were there, "This man too was with Jesus the Nazarene."
verses.26:72: And again he denied it with an oath: "I do not know the man."
verses.26:73: And after a little while, those who were standing there approached and said to Peter, "Truly you too are one of them, for even your speech reveals you."
verses.26:74: Then he began to invoke curses and swear that he did not know the man. And at once a rooster crowed.
verses.26:75: And Peter remembered the word of Jesus that He had spoken: "Before a rooster crows, you will deny Me three times." And going outside, he wept bitterly.
verses.27:1: Now when morning had come, all the chief priests and the elders of the people held a consultation against Jesus, so that they might hand Him over to death.
verses.27:2: And having bound Him, they brought Him and handed Him over to Pontius Pilate, the governor.
verses.27:3: Then when Judas, who had handed Him over, saw that He had been condemned, he was moved by repentance and brought back the thirty silver coins to the chief priests and the elders,
verses.27:4: saying, "I have sinned in handing over righteous blood." But they said, "What is that to us? You see to it."
verses.27:5: And having thrown down the silver coins in the temple, he withdrew; and going away, he hanged himself with a noose.
verses.27:6: Now the chief priests, having taken the silver coins, said, "It is not permitted to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood."
verses.27:7: And having held a consultation, they bought the potter's field with them for the burial of foreigners.
verses.27:8: For this reason that field has been called Akeldama, that is, Field of Blood, down to the present day.
verses.27:9: Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, saying, "And they took the thirty silver coins, the price of Him who was valued, whom they valued from the sons of Israel,
verses.27:10: and they gave them for the potter's field, just as the Lord appointed for me."
verses.27:11: Now Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor questioned Him, saying, "Are You the King of the Jews?" Jesus said to him, "You say so."
verses.27:12: And while He was being accused by the chief priests and the elders, He answered nothing.
verses.27:13: Then Pilate said to Him, "Do You not hear how many testimonies they are speaking against You?"
verses.27:14: And He did not answer him regarding a single word, so that the governor marveled greatly.
verses.27:15: Now during the feast day the governor was accustomed to release to the people one prisoner whom they wished;
verses.27:16: and at that time he had a notorious prisoner who was called Barabbas.
verses.27:17: Therefore when they had assembled, Pilate said, "Whom do you want me to release to you: Barabbas, or Jesus, who is called Christ?"
verses.27:18: For he knew that they had handed Him over through envy.
verses.27:19: Now while he was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent word to him, saying, "Have no dealings with that righteous man, for I have suffered many things today in a vision because of Him."
verses.27:20: But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowds that they should ask for Barabbas, but destroy Jesus.
verses.27:21: Now the governor answered and said to them, "Which of the two do you want to be released to you?" But they said, "Barabbas."
verses.27:22: Pilate said to them, "What then should I do with Jesus, who is called Christ?"
verses.27:23: They all said, "Let Him be crucified!" The governor said to them, "What evil, then, has He done?" But they kept shouting all the more, saying, "Let Him be crucified!"
verses.27:24: Now when Pilate saw that he was making no headway, but rather that an uproar was arising, he took water and washed his hands before the people, saying, "I am innocent of the blood of this righteous man; you yourselves see to it."
verses.27:25: And the entire people answered and said, "His blood be on us and on our children!"
verses.27:26: Then he released Barabbas to them; but after Jesus had been flogged, he handed Him over to them to be crucified.
verses.27:27: Then the soldiers of the governor, taking Jesus into the praetorium, assembled the entire cohort around Him;
verses.27:28: and stripping Him, they placed a scarlet cloak around Him,
verses.27:29: and weaving a crown of thorns, they set it on His head, and a reed in His right hand. And bending the knee before Him, they were mocking Him, saying, "Hail, King of the Jews!"
verses.27:30: And spitting on Him, they took the reed and kept striking His head.
verses.27:31: And after they had mocked Him, they stripped Him of the cloak and dressed Him in His garments, and they led Him away so that they might crucify Him.
verses.27:32: Now as they were going out, they found a Cyrenian man, Simon by name; they forced this man to bear His cross.
verses.27:33: And they came to a place that is called Golgotha, which is the Place of a Skull.
verses.27:34: And they gave Him wine mixed with gall to drink. And after tasting it, He refused to drink.
verses.27:35: Now after they had crucified Him, they divided His garments, casting lots, so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying, "They divided My garments among themselves, and over My garment they cast lots."
verses.27:36: And sitting down, they kept watch over Him.
verses.27:37: And they placed above His head the written charge against Him: "This is Jesus, the King of the Jews."
verses.27:38: Then two bandits were crucified with Him, one on the right and one on the left.
verses.27:39: Now those passing by were blaspheming Him, shaking their heads,
verses.27:40: and saying, "Aha! You who destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days, save Yourself! If You are the Son of God, come down from the cross!"
verses.27:41: Likewise the chief priests also, mocking with the scribes and the elders, were saying,
verses.27:42: "He saved others; He is not able to save Himself. If He is the King of Israel, let Him come down now from the cross, and we believe Him.
verses.27:43: He trusts in God; let Him deliver Him now, if He desires Him; for He said, 'I am the Son of God.'"
verses.27:44: Now the bandits who had been crucified with Him were also reproaching Him with the very same thing.
verses.27:45: Now from the sixth hour, darkness came over the entire earth until the ninth hour.
verses.27:46: And around the ninth hour, Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying, "Eli, Eli, lamma sabacthani?" that is, "My God, My God, why have You abandoned Me?"
verses.27:47: Now some of those standing there, hearing it, were saying, "This man is calling Elijah."
verses.27:48: And at once one of them ran, took a sponge and filled it with vinegar, and placed it on a reed, and was offering it to Him to drink.
verses.27:49: But the rest were saying, "Wait, let us see whether Elijah comes to deliver Him."
verses.27:50: Now Jesus, crying out again with a loud voice, released His spirit.
verses.27:51: And look, the veil of the temple was torn into two parts from top to bottom; and the earth shook, and the rocks were split,
verses.27:52: and the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep rose up.
verses.27:53: And going out from the tombs after His resurrection, they came into the holy city and appeared to many.
verses.27:54: Now the centurion and those who were with him guarding Jesus, having seen the earthquake and the things that were happening, feared greatly, saying, "Truly this man was the Son of God!"
verses.27:55: Now many women were there at a distance, who had followed Jesus from Galilee, serving Him,
verses.27:56: among whom was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
verses.27:57: Now when evening had come, a certain rich man from Arimathea came, Joseph by name, who himself was also a disciple of Jesus;
verses.27:58: this man approached Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus. Then Pilate ordered the body to be handed over.
verses.27:59: And having taken the body, Joseph wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,
verses.27:60: and placed it in his new tomb, which he had carved out in the rock. And he rolled a large stone up to the doorway of the tomb, and departed.
verses.27:61: Now Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting across from the grave.
verses.27:62: Now on the following day, which is after the Preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees came together to Pilate,
verses.27:63: saying, "Sir, we remember that while still alive, that deceiver said, 'After three days I will rise again.'
verses.27:64: Therefore order the grave to be guarded until the third day; otherwise His disciples might come and steal Him away and say to the people, 'He has risen from the dead,' and the final deception will be worse than the first."
verses.27:65: Pilate said to them, "You have a guard; go, guard it as you know how."
verses.27:66: So they departed and secured the grave, sealing the stone, together with the guards.
verses.28:1: Now in the evening of the Sabbath, as it was growing light toward the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
verses.28:2: And look, a great earthquake took place. For an angel of the Lord descended from heaven and, approaching, rolled back the stone and was sitting on it.
verses.28:3: Now his appearance was like lightning, and his garment like snow.
verses.28:4: And out of fear of him, the guards were terrified and became like dead men.
verses.28:5: But the angel answered and said to the women, "As for you, do not be afraid, for I know that you are seeking Jesus, who was crucified.
verses.28:6: He is not here; for He has risen, just as He said. Come and see the place where the Lord had been laid.
verses.28:7: And going quickly, tell His disciples that He has risen. And look, He is going ahead of you into Galilee; there you will see Him. Look, I have told you beforehand."
verses.28:8: And they went out quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, running to bring word to His disciples.
verses.28:9: And look, Jesus met them, saying, "Greetings!" And they approached and grasped His feet and worshiped Him.
verses.28:10: Then Jesus said to them, "Do not be afraid. Go, bring word to My brothers that they should go into Galilee; there they will see Me."
verses.28:11: Now when they had departed, look, some of the guards came into the city and reported to the chief priests all the things that had taken place.
verses.28:12: And having assembled with the elders and taken counsel, they gave a large amount of money to the soldiers,
verses.28:13: saying, "Say, 'His disciples came at night and stole Him while we were sleeping.'
verses.28:14: And if this is heard by the governor, we will persuade him and make you secure."
verses.28:15: So they, having accepted the money, did just as they had been instructed. And this account has been spread widely among the Jews up to this present day.
verses.28:16: Now the eleven disciples departed into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had directed them.
verses.28:17: And seeing Him, they worshiped; but some doubted.
verses.28:18: And approaching, Jesus spoke to them, saying, "All power has been given to Me in heaven and on earth.
verses.28:19: Therefore go and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit,
verses.28:20: teaching them to keep everything that I have commanded you. And look, I am with you every day, even to the consummation of the age."

notes.1:6: The Clementine Vulgate reads "David autem rex" ("David the king"), retaining the royal title here, and literally refers to Bathsheba as "ex ea quæ fuit Uriæ" ("her who had been Uriah's") without supplying the word "wife."
notes.1:18: The Clementine Vulgate reads simply "Christi" ("of Christ") rather than "of Jesus Christ," and uses "in utero habens" (literally "having in the womb," i.e., pregnant), matching "in utero habebit" in v. 23.
notes.1:20: Latin "natum est" (literally "has been born" or "has come into being") renders Greek "gennēthen" ("begotten/conceived"), translated here as "has been conceived" to fit the prenatal context.
notes.1:25: The Clementine Vulgate reads "filium suum primogenitum" ("her firstborn son"), preserving the fuller reading alongside the imperfect tense "non cognoscebat" ("did not know").
notes.2:1: The Clementine Vulgate reads "in Bethlehem Juda" ("in Bethlehem of Judah"; likewise "Judæ" in v. 5) rather than "Judea" (contrast "Judæa" in 2:22, 3:1, and 3:5).
notes.2:6: The Clementine Vulgate reads "qui regat" ("who will rule/govern") rather than the Greek verb meaning "will shepherd."
notes.2:11: The Clementine Vulgate reads "invenerunt" ("they found") rather than "they saw," a distinct reading established in the Latin textual tradition.
notes.2:12: Latin "responso accepto" literally means "having received an answer," a common Vulgate idiom for a divine reply or directive (contrast "admonitus," "warned," in v. 22).
notes.3:2: Latin "Pœnitentiam agite" literally means "do repentance," the standard Vulgate idiom for "repent" and lexically linked to "pœnitentia" ("repentance") in vv. 8 and 11.
notes.3:10: The Clementine Vulgate uses future passive verbs ("excidetur, et in ignem mittetur," "will be cut down and thrown into the fire") where the Greek text uses present-tense verbs.
notes.3:12: The Clementine Vulgate reads simply "in horreum" ("into the granary") without a possessive pronoun ("his").
notes.3:17: Latin "in quo mihi complacui" (literally "in whom I have pleased Myself") uses the perfect tense with the reflexive dative "mihi."
notes.4:6: Vulgate reads the perfect tense "mandavit" ("He has commanded"), matching the Vulgate Psalter (Psalm 90:11 [91:11]), whereas the Greek text of Matthew has the future tense ("He will command").
notes.4:16: Vulgate reads "in regione umbrae mortis" ("in the region of the shadow of death"), whereas the Greek text coordinates both nouns ("in the region and shadow of death").
notes.4:17: Latin poenitentiam agite literally means "do repentance," the Vulgate idiom for Greek metanoeite; it is rendered "Repent" here, as in 3:2, where the Latin is identical.
notes.4:22: Vulgate reads "relictis retibus" ("having left their nets"), whereas the Greek text has "leaving the boat."
notes.4:24: Latin "lunaticos" literally means "moonstruck," a term anciently used for people suffering from epilepsy or periodic seizures.
notes.5:5: Latin possidebunt ("will possess") reflects the Vulgate wording rather than the Greek verb meaning "inherit."
notes.5:21: Latin occides ... occiderit means "kill," rendered the same way as non occides in Mark 10:19 and Luke 18:20; in Matthew 19:18 the Vulgate instead reads homicidium ("murder").
notes.5:22: Raca is an Aramaic term of contempt, and gehennae ignis ("the Gehenna of fire") retains the Latin loanword referring to the Valley of Hinnom as an image of fiery judgment.
notes.5:26: A quadrans was the smallest Roman bronze coin, worth one-quarter of an as.
notes.5:37: Latin a malo can be understood either as neuter "from evil" or masculine "from the evil one," and the same ambiguity occurs with malo in 5:39.
notes.5:44: The Vulgate preserves the fuller clauses benefacite his qui oderunt vos ("do good to those who hate you") and et calumniantibus vos ("and slander you"), which are absent from most modern critical Greek editions; in 5:45 the Vulgate also reads super bonos et malos ("on the good and the evil") rather than the Greek order "the evil and the good."
notes.6:11: Vulgate-distinct reading: Jerome coined supersubstantialem ("supersubstantial" or "above-essential") to render Greek epiousion here, whereas in Luke 11:3 he translated the same Greek term as quotidianum ("daily").
notes.6:13: Latin a malo can mean either "from evil" (neuter) or "from the evil one" (masculine). The Clementine Vulgate ends the prayer with "Amen" without the liturgical doxology found in later Greek manuscripts.
notes.6:19: The Vulgate places "rust" (aerugo) before "moth" (tinea), reversing the Greek order ("moth and rust"), and uses effodiunt (literally "dig through") for thieves breaking through mud-brick walls.
notes.6:24: Latin sustinebit literally means "will uphold" or "will bear with," and mammonae ("mammon") preserves an Aramaic loanword referring to wealth or money.
notes.6:27: The Vulgate uses cogitans ("by thinking"), differing from sollicitus ("anxious") in nearby verses, and staturam, which specifically means physical height ("stature") rather than lifespan.
notes.7:14: The Vulgate reads the exclamation Quam ("How narrow...!"), corresponding to the Greek variant ti, where many Greek manuscripts read causal hoti ("For/Because the gate is narrow").
notes.7:17: The Vulgate uses the same adjective malus ("bad") for both the tree and its fruits, whereas the Greek distinguishes sapron ("diseased/rotten") for the tree from ponerous ("bad/evil") for the fruit.
notes.7:21: Vulgate-distinct addition: the Clementine Vulgate includes the concluding clause "he himself will enter the kingdom of heaven" (ipse intrabit in regnum caelorum), which is absent from most standard Greek editions.
notes.7:29: Vulgate-distinct addition: the Clementine Vulgate adds "and the Pharisees" (et pharisaei) after "their scribes," a reading attested in Latin tradition and some Greek manuscripts but absent from most critical Greek texts.
notes.8:6: Latin "puer" literally means "boy" and was commonly used for a young household servant, distinct from "servus" ("servant") in 8:9.
notes.8:9: The Vulgate includes the participle "constitutus" ("placed/set") after "sub potestate," which is absent from most Greek manuscripts of Matthew 8:9 (compare Luke 7:8).
notes.8:15: The Vulgate reads plural "eis" ("them") rather than singular "Him," which appears in many Greek manuscripts.
notes.8:28: The Vulgate reads "Gerasenorum" ("of the Gerasenes"), whereas Greek manuscripts of Matthew commonly read "Gadarenes" or "Gergesenes."
notes.8:30: The Vulgate distinctly reads "non longe ab illis" ("not far from them"), contrasting with the Greek reading "at a distance from them."
notes.9:4: The Vulgate reads "vidisset" ("had seen") rather than "knowing," reflecting the Greek textual variant "idon" instead of "eidos."
notes.9:15: Latin "filii sponsi" ("sons of the bridegroom") literally preserves a Semitic idiom referring to the bridegroom's attendants or wedding guests.
notes.9:16: In the Vulgate, "plenitudinem" ("fullness") is accusative as the direct object of "tollit," indicating that the patch pulls away the garment's substance and creates a worse tear.
notes.9:18: The Vulgate includes the address "Domine" ("Lord"), which is absent from the Greek text of Matthew 9:18.
notes.9:28: The Vulgate adds "vobis" ("for you") to Jesus's question, whereas the Greek text omits it.
notes.10:4: Latin "Chananæus" transliterates Greek "Kananaios" (from Aramaic for "zealot") with the Vulgate spelling for "Canaanite"; it is rendered "Cananaean" here rather than harmonized to "Zealot" from Luke 6:15.
notes.10:5: The Vulgate has the plural "civitates" ("cities"), whereas the Greek text has the singular "city."
notes.10:12: The Clementine Vulgate includes "dicentes: Pax huic domui" ("saying, 'Peace to this house'"), a clause absent from critical Greek editions.
notes.10:25: The Vulgate preserves the spelling "Beelzebub" (echoing 2 Kings 1:2) rather than the Greek form "Beelzebul."
notes.10:42: The Vulgate uses the superlative "minimis" ("least ones"), whereas the Greek uses the positive adjective "little ones."
notes.11:2: The Vulgate reads "in vinculis" ("in chains") rather than "in prison," and "duos de discipulis suis" ("two of his disciples") rather than critical Greek "by his disciples."
notes.11:19: The Vulgate reads "a filiis suis" ("by her children"), whereas modern critical Greek editions read "by her deeds."
notes.11:20: The Vulgate phrase "pœnitentiam agere" (here and in 11:21) literally means "to perform repentance" and serves as the regular Latin equivalent for "repent."
notes.11:23: The Vulgate adds "forte" ("perhaps it would have remained") in rendering the Greek conditional particle, and uses "infernum" ("the underworld," distinct from "gehennam" in 10:28) for Greek "Hades."
notes.11:28: The Vulgate uses "reficiam" ("refresh" or "restore") here rather than repeating "rest" ("requiem," 11:29), and in 11:30 describes the yoke as "suave" ("sweet" or "pleasant").
notes.12:6: The Vulgate uses the masculine comparative adjective major ("One greater"), whereas critical Greek texts read the neuter meizon ("something greater"); contrast the neuter plus ("something greater") in 12:41-42.
notes.12:8: The Vulgate includes etiam ("even"), reflecting the traditional Byzantine Greek reading (kai tou sabbatou) rather than modern critical Greek editions that omit the word.
notes.12:24: The Vulgate retains the spelling Beelzebub (here and in 12:27), echoing the Old Testament Baal-zebub (2 Kings 1:2), whereas critical Greek manuscripts read Beelzeboul (Beelzebul).
notes.12:41: The Latin idiom poenitentiam egerunt (literally "did repentance") is Jerome's standard rendering of the Greek verb metanoeo ("repent").
notes.12:47: The Vulgate reads simply quaerentes te ("seeking You"), shorter than most Greek manuscripts that add "to speak to you"; several early Greek manuscripts omit verse 47 altogether.
notes.13:9: The Vulgate includes the gerund audiendi ("to hear") here and in 13:43, whereas the critical Greek text simply reads "ears" without "to hear."
notes.13:25: Latin zizania denotes darnel (Lolium temulentum), a noxious weed closely resembling wheat until maturity; it is rendered "weeds" to preserve the Latin plural grammar across the parable.
notes.13:47: The Vulgate explicitly adds piscium ("of fish") in ex omni genere piscium, where the Greek text reads simply "of every kind."
notes.13:48: The Clementine Vulgate reads the dative/ablative form bonis where accusative bonos ("the good ones," parallel to malos, "the bad ones") is grammatically expected and found in older Vulgate manuscripts.
notes.13:54: The Vulgate reads plural in synagogis eorum ("in their synagogues"), whereas the Greek text has singular "in their synagogue."
notes.14:3: The Clementine Vulgate reads simply "his brother's wife" (uxorem fratris sui), omitting the name "Philip" found in most Greek manuscripts.
notes.14:21: The Vulgate states "five thousand men" (quinque millia virorum) without the qualifying "about" present in the Greek text.
notes.14:24: The Clementine Vulgate reads "in the middle of the sea" (in medio mari), agreeing with the Byzantine Greek tradition, whereas critical Greek editions read "already many stadia from the land."
notes.14:29: The Vulgate has a purpose clause ("in order to come to Jesus," ut veniret ad Jesum) and singular "water" (aquam, contrasting with plural aquas in 14:28), whereas critical Greek editions read "and came to Jesus" with plural "waters" in both verses.
notes.14:34: The Clementine Vulgate reads the shorter place name "Genesar" (rendered "Gennesar," as in 1 Maccabees 11:67) and "into the land of Gennesar," whereas the Greek text reads "Gennesaret."
notes.15:5: The Vulgate renders the elliptical Greek clause as a complete statement, "Whatever gift is from me will benefit you" (Latin Munus, quodcumque est ex me, tibi proderit). In 15:6, the Clementine Vulgate also includes "or his mother" and reads "commandment" (mandatum) where critical Greek editions read "word."
notes.15:9: The Clementine Vulgate includes "and" (et) in docentes doctrinas et mandata hominum ("teaching the doctrines and commandments of men"), whereas the Greek reads "teaching as doctrines the commandments of men."
notes.15:26: Unlike the Greek, which uses the diminutive kynaria ("little dogs") in both 15:26 and 15:27, the Vulgate distinguishes canibus ("dogs") in Jesus's reply from the diminutive catelli ("puppies" or "little dogs") in the woman's response.
notes.15:31: Unlike most Greek manuscripts, the Clementine Vulgate omits "the crippled made whole" from the list of miracles witnessed by the crowd, naming only the mute speaking, the lame walking, and the blind seeing.
notes.15:39: The Vulgate reads Magedan (Magadan), agreeing with the earliest Greek witnesses against the later Textus Receptus reading "Magdala."
notes.16:4: In the Clementine Vulgate verse division, the sentence about discerning the sky and the signs of the times opens verse 4 rather than concluding verse 3. The Vulgate also retains the weather saying in 16:2-3 and includes "the prophet" after Jonah.
notes.16:18: The Latin preserves the wordplay between Petrus ("Peter") and petram ("rock"). Inferi denotes the underworld or realm of the dead (rendering Greek Hades), distinct from gehenna.
notes.16:20: The Clementine Vulgate reads Jesus Christus ("Jesus Christ"), whereas most critical Greek texts omit "Jesus" and read simply "the Christ."
notes.16:25: Across 16:25-26, the Latin uses the single noun anima four times, rendered "life" in 16:25 and "soul" in 16:26.
notes.16:27: The Vulgate reads plural opera ("works"), whereas the Greek uses the singular praxin ("deed" or "conduct").
notes.17:2: The Vulgate reads "sicut nix" ("like snow"), whereas most modern critical Greek texts read "as light."
notes.17:4: The Vulgate uses the first-person plural "faciamus" ("let us make"), matching the Byzantine tradition rather than the singular ("I will make") found in most modern critical Greek texts.
notes.17:14: The Vulgate reads singular "cum venisset" ("when He had come") rather than plural "when they had come."
notes.17:15: In the Latin text this verse is included in verse 14. "Moonstruck" literally renders Latin "lunaticus," an ancient term for periodic seizures or epilepsy.
notes.17:20: The Vulgate reads "incredulitatem" ("unbelief") and includes the emphatic particle "quippe" ("for indeed"), whereas most modern critical Greek editions read "little faith."
notes.17:27: A "stater" was a silver coin worth four drachmas, exactly covering the "didrachma" (the two-drachma temple tax in 17:24) for both Jesus and Peter.
notes.18:1: The Vulgate adds parenthetical "putas" ("do you think") and uses comparative "major" ("greater") with superlative force ("the greatest"), as also in 18:4.
notes.18:6: Literally "mola asinaria," a large heavy millstone turned by a donkey rather than a small hand mill.
notes.18:9: The Vulgate retains the loanword "gehennam" ("Gehenna," the Valley of Hinnom, symbolizing the place of final fiery punishment), and uses positive "bonum ... quam" ("good ... than") with comparative force ("better ... than"), as in 18:8.
notes.18:22: Latin "septuagies septies" literally means "seventy times seven" (490), though the underlying idiom echoing Genesis 4:24 is also understood by some as "seventy-seven times."
notes.18:27: The Vulgate repeats the same verb "dimisit" ("released him and forgave him the debt"), linking the servant's physical release with the cancellation of his debt.
notes.19:4: The Clementine Vulgate explicitly reads qui fecit hominem ab initio ("He who made man from the beginning"), whereas Greek manuscripts omit "man" here.
notes.19:17: Combining Magister bone ("Good Teacher") in verse 16 with Quid me interrogas de bono? ("Why do you question Me about what is good?"), the Vulgate explicitly adds Deus ("God") in Unus est bonus, Deus ("One is good: God").
notes.19:24: The Clementine Vulgate reads in regnum caelorum ("into the kingdom of heaven"), whereas Greek manuscripts read "the kingdom of God" here.
notes.19:28: The Vulgate renders the phrase in sede majestatis suae ("on the throne of His majesty"), where the Greek text has "glory."
notes.19:29: The Vulgate has singular domum ("house"), includes aut uxorem ("or wife"), and renders possidebit ("will possess") where the Greek has "will inherit."
notes.20:15: The Clementine Vulgate reads Aut non licet mihi quod volo, facere? ("Or is it not lawful for me to do what I wish?"), omitting the Greek phrase "with what belongs to me." The idiom "your eye evil" (oculus tuus nequam) denotes envy or stinginess.
notes.20:16: The Vulgate includes the concluding sentence Multi enim sunt vocati, pauci vero electi ("For many are called, yet few are chosen"), which is absent from many early Greek manuscripts here.
notes.20:23: The Vulgate explicitly reads dare vobis ("to give to you"), whereas critical Greek texts omit "to you."
notes.20:34: The Vulgate reads simply viderunt ("they saw"), whereas the underlying Greek verb means "regained their sight" or "looked up."
notes.21:5: Latin 'filium subjugalis' is literally 'the son of one under the yoke,' referring to the young of a yoked draft animal or beast of burden.
notes.21:7: The Vulgate reads 'eum desuper sedere fecerunt' ('had Him sit on top'), using a plural causative verb rather than the singular 'He sat' found in most modern critical Greek editions.
notes.21:21: Latin 'Tolle, et jacta te' uses active and reflexive imperatives ('Lift yourself up and throw yourself') where Greek manuscripts have passive imperatives ('Be taken up and be thrown').
notes.21:30: The Vulgate renders the second son's reply as 'Eo, domine' ('I am going, sir'), using the verb 'to go' where the Greek text has the pronoun 'Ego' ('I [will], sir').
notes.21:41: Latin 'Malos male perdet' preserves a sharp wordplay on 'malus' (literally 'the wicked ones he will wickedly/miserably destroy').
notes.22:7: The Clementine Vulgate includes the clause "when he heard this" (cum audisset), reflecting Byzantine and Western Greek witnesses, whereas modern critical Greek editions omit it.
notes.22:24: The Vulgate reads singular "a son" (filium), whereas the Greek text reads plural "children" (tekna).
notes.22:30: The Vulgate retains "of God" (angeli Dei) and uses future-tense verbs throughout (nubent, nubentur, erunt), whereas modern critical Greek editions omit "of God."
notes.22:37: The Vulgate shifts from "from" (ex) with the heart to "in" (in) with the soul and mind, whereas the Greek text repeats a single preposition.
notes.22:44: The Vulgate reads "a footstool for Your feet" (scabellum pedum tuorum, agreeing with Psalm 109:1 [110:1] and majority Greek witnesses), whereas modern critical Greek editions read "underneath Your feet."
notes.23:10: The Clementine Vulgate uses the same Latin noun magister ("teacher" or "master") in both verses 8 and 10, whereas the Greek distinguishes didaskalos (v. 8) and kathegetes (v. 10).
notes.23:16: Latin debet (also in v. 18) literally means "owes" or "is indebted," here signifying being bound to fulfill the oath.
notes.23:25: Unlike Greek manuscripts that read third-person plural ("they are full," referring to the cup and dish) with "self-indulgence," the Vulgate reads second-person plural pleni estis ("you are full") and immunditia ("uncleanness"), directly contrasting with mundatis ("you clean") and mundum ("clean," v. 26).
notes.23:37: The Vulgate maintains second-person singular address throughout (occidis, lapidas, ad te, noluisti) and punctuates the verse as a rhetorical question, whereas the Greek shifts to third-person "to her" and ends with second-person plural.
notes.23:38: The Vulgate uses the future passive relinquetur ("will be left") and includes deserta ("desolate"), whereas many Greek manuscripts use the present passive ("is left").
notes.24:2: Latin Videtis haec omnia? ("Do you see all these things?") is an affirmative question without the negation ("Do you not see...?") found in the Greek text.
notes.24:7: The Clementine Vulgate includes pestilentiae ("plagues") and places it before fames ("famines"), whereas critical Greek editions omit "plagues" and Byzantine manuscripts list "famines" first.
notes.24:31: Latin cum tuba, et voce magna ("with a trumpet and a loud voice") coordinates two nouns with et, whereas Greek critical texts read "with a loud trumpet" (and Byzantine texts read "with a trumpet of a great sound").
notes.24:36: The Clementine Vulgate reads only neque angeli caelorum, nisi solus Pater ("not even the angels of the heavens, except the Father alone"), without "nor the Son," agreeing with the Byzantine Greek manuscripts; critical Greek editions include it.
notes.24:42: Both here (qua hora, "at what hour") and in verse 43 (qua hora), the Clementine Vulgate reads "hour," whereas critical Greek texts read "what day" in verse 42 and "what watch" in verse 43.
